  - [0xA] (offset +10): Viewport X dimension (will be grid-aligned to 8-pixel cells)
  - [0xB] (offset +11): Viewport Y dimension (will be grid-aligned to 8-pixel cells)
  - [0x47C] (offset +1148): Flag determining border height mode

Returns:
- void (no return value)

Special Cases:
- Magic number 0x47C at offset 1148 bytes controls border height calculation
- Midpoint detection: nX/2 triggers alternate sprite rendering
- Sprite IDs 0x280-0x285 are hardcoded border frame sprites
- Grid size: 8-pixel cells (>> 3 operation)
- Note: Function uses loop iteration variables optimized to registers (not visible as named variables)

functions.name: ShuffleAndRenderGridCells
functions.signature: void ShuffleAndRenderGridCells(int iGridCtx, int nMinOffset, int nGridWidth, int nMaxRenderCount)
functions.comment:
Shuffle grid cells and render valid positions with offset

Algorithm:
1. Load grid dimensions from pGridData: width from offset 0x5c, height from offset 0x60
2. Calculate total grid size (width * height) to determine shuffle count
3. If grid is empty, exit (skip rendering)
4. Allocate memory for grid coordinate pairs [x, y] via Ordinal_10045
5. Populate coordinate array: iterate 0 to grid_size, store (index % width, index / width) for each cell
6. Shuffle coordinates: generate random indices twice (Ordinal_10918) and swap coordinate pairs
7. Iterate shuffled coordinates, render valid cells:
   - Get coordinates [x, y] from shuffled array
   - Calculate random offset (or 0 if nOffsetAdjusted = 0)
   - Call ValidateGridRectangle with grid bounds [x, y + nMinOffset + nOffsetAdjusted]
   - If valid, render with RenderObjectAtCoordinates, increment render counter
   - Stop if nMaxRenderCount cells rendered (exit code 0xe7, else 0xee)
8. Free memory via Ordinal_10046

Parameters:
  pGridData - Pointer to grid structure with width/height offsets
  nMinOffset - Base Y-axis offset for grid validation
  nGridWidth - Grid width in cells (not used directly; derived from pGridData)
  nMaxRenderCount - Maximum cells to render; 0 = render all

Returns:
  void; sets exit code via Ordinal_10046: 0xee (success) or 0xe7 (max rendered)

Special Cases:
  - Empty grid (size = 0) skips all processing
  - nOffsetAdjusted = 0 skips random offset generation
  - nMaxRenderCount = 0 renders all valid cells found

functions.name: RenderViewportPanel
functions.comment:
Renders viewport panel content based on panel type.

Algorithm:
1. Load panel type from pViewport[1]
2. For type 0x4f: Render frame with grid points and entity overlays
3. For type 0x50: Render border with corner objects and grid points
4. For type 0x51: Render border at calculated Y offset with corner objects
5. For type 0x52: Render default object at origin (0x28c)
6. Calculate scaled coordinates by signed division: (nValue + (nValue >> 31 & 0x7)) >> 3
7. Subtract 4 pixel offset for final rendering coordinates

Parameters:
pViewport (int *) - Pointer to viewport structure containing:
  [1] - Panel type (0x4f/0x50/0x51/0x52)
  [10] - Base X coordinate (signed 32-bit)
  [11] - Base Y coordinate (signed 32-bit)

Returns:
void - No return value

Magic Numbers:
0x4f - Panel frame type identifier
0x50 - Viewport border type identifier
0x51 - Dynamic border type identifier
0x52 - Default object type identifier
0x277, 0x275, 0x286, 0x28c - Graphic resource IDs
0x3 - Default object dimension (3x3 pixels)
0xf - Full opacity mask value

functions.name: RenderGameViewport
functions.comment:
Renders the game viewport with viewpoint objects and optional UI elements.

Algorithm:
1. Call FUN_6fd91740 to perform viewport initialization
2. Render viewpoint objects using RenderViewpointObjects()
3. Render viewport panel using RenderViewportPanel()
4. If viewport flag [pViewport + 0x4] == 0x53, render 6 UI objects:
   - Objects 0, 2, 6 at Y offset 0 with texture IDs 0x28D, 0x28E, 0x28F
   - Objects 0, 2, 6 at Y offset 4 with texture IDs 0x290, 0x291, 0x292
5. Return to caller

Parameters:
pViewport (int *): Pointer to viewport structure
  - pViewport[0]: Viewport state/identifier
  - pViewport[1]: Viewport flags (0x53 enables UI element rendering)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- UI elements (texture IDs 0x28D-0x292) only render when flag is exactly 0x53
- All RenderObjectAtCoordinates calls use -1 as quality/layer parameter

functions.name: FindPathBetweenCoordinates
functions.comment:
Find optimal path between two tile coordinates using A* pathfinding search

Algorithm:
1. Initialize: FUN_6fdd5de0() loads global context (map data, viewport)
2. Calculate initial tile coordinates from pixel offsets using viewport base
3. Compute Manhattan distance between start and end coordinates
4. Quick path check: if distance < 2 tiles, use simple direct placement (return 1)
5. Main search loop: Compute heuristic cost using distance tables g_abDeltaXTable
6. Initialize open list with 10 stack-allocated node slots, max 900 nodes total
7. While search not exhausted: pop from open list, check adjacent cells via direction offsets
   - For each neighbor: calculate movement cost, heuristic, check walkability vs obstacles (0x200 flag)
   - ValidateCoordinateRange() ensures tile within bounds; GetNestedArrayElement() checks tile flags
   - If better path found, add to open list; track parent node for path reconstruction
8. If goal reached (coordinates match), reconstruct path by walking parent chain
   - Call InitializeMemoryBlock() to allocate each path node, populate with coordinates
9. If search limit reached (900 nodes) before goal, return 0 (no path)
10. Return 1 on success with path nodes populated in memory blocks

Parameters:
- Implicit: Uses global map state loaded by FUN_6fdd5de0
- Implicit: Uses viewport context (ECX register), target coordinates (EDX/EBX, EAX registers)

Returns:
- 1 (EAX): Path found and reconstructed
- 0 (EAX): No path exists or search exhausted 900 node limit

Special Cases:
- Adjacent tiles (distance < 2): bypass search, direct placement
- Impassable obstacles (flag & 0x200): mark as visited, skip in expansion
- Node pool exhaustion (>900): terminate early, return 0
- Closed list tracking via piVar12[5] (visited flag) prevents re-expansion

Structure Layout (PathNode - 40 bytes):
  Offset | Size | Field Name          | Type    | Description
  0x00   | 4    | nCost               | int     | Total cost (heuristic + movement)
  0x04   | 4    | nMovementCost       | int     | Accumulated movement cost
  0x08   | 4    | nHeuristic          | int     | Heuristic distance to goal
  0x0c   | 4    | nX                  | int     | Tile X coordinate
  0x10   | 4    | nY                  | int     | Tile Y coordinate
  0x14   | 4    | nVisited            | int     | Visited counter (0-3 states)
  0x18   | 4    | pDirectionOffsets   | byte *  | Pointer to direction offset table
  0x1c   | 1    | chDirection         | byte    | Current search direction (0-3)
  0x20   | 4    | pParent             | int *   | Parent node pointer for path reconstruction

functions.name: LookupTableValue
functions.signature: uint LookupTableValue(int nX, int nY, int nTableSelector)
functions.comment:
Lookup table value from indexed coordinate tables.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate index base using: nX + nY * 3
2. Fetch lookup value from g_pdwIndexLookupTable at calculated index
3. Branch on nTableSelector:
   - If nTableSelector > 3: Offset = nTableSelector - 4 + (lookup * 2), return from g_pdwHighValueTable
   - Otherwise: Offset = nTableSelector + (lookup * 4), return from g_pdwLowValueTable
4. Return 32-bit value from selected table at calculated offset

Parameters:
int nX - X coordinate component for index calculation
int nY - Y coordinate component (multiplied by 3 for stride)
int nTableSelector - Table selector determining which table and offset calculation

Returns:
uint - 32-bit value retrieved from selected table at calculated offset

Special Cases:
Magic numbers indicate table index arithmetic (multiplies by 3, 2, 4 for different strides and offsets)
Branching point at 0x4 threshold suggests alternate lookup algorithms for different selector ranges

functions.name: GetLookupTableValue
functions.signature: uint GetLookupTableValue(int nCoordX, int nParam2, int nCoordY, int nTableIndex, int nAccessMode)
functions.comment:
Retrieves a value from lookup tables indexed by coordinates and access mode.

Algorithm:
1. Normalize nCoordX: if negative, subtract 2; if positive, add 2 (center bias)
2. Normalize nCoordY: if negative, subtract 2; if positive, add 2 (center bias)
3. Calculate composite index: (nCoordY + nTableIndex) * 9 + nCoordX + nParam2
4. Look up index value in g_adwLookupIndexTable at calculated offset
5. If lookup value == -1 (invalid), return 0
6. If nAccessMode > 3, access g_adwHighAccessModeTable with offset (nAccessMode - 6 + value * 2)
7. Otherwise, access g_adwStandardAccessTable with offset (nAccessMode + value * 4)

Parameters:
  nCoordX - First coordinate (signed), normalized with +/-2 bias
  nParam2 - Additive parameter for index calculation
  nCoordY - Second coordinate (signed), normalized with +/-2 bias
  nTableIndex - Base table selection index
  nAccessMode - Access mode selector (0-based): >3 uses high table, <=3 uses standard

Returns:
  uint - Table lookup result, or 0 if lookup index is -1 (invalid)

functions.name: ProcessArrayElementFlags
functions.comment:
Iterate 2D array structure and process elements with flag bits set.

Algorithm:
1. Load array descriptor base address from param offset 0x38 and 0x2c
2. Initialize 8 dimension/stride parameters from stack (local_3c, local_38, local_34, local_30, local_2c, local_28, local_24, local_20, local_1c, local_18, local_14, local_10, local_c, local_8, local_4)
3. Set nLoopCount = 4 (process 4 nested loop iterations)
4. For each iteration: read dimension params from pointer array (pdwDimensionParams)
5. Validate row and column indices against array bounds at offset 0x5c and 0x60
6. Outer loop: call GetNestedArrayElement(array, row, col) to get element
7. While element has flag bit clear (element & 1 == 0), process element:
   - Inner loop: increment row by dwRowStride, fetch element again
   - While nested element flag clear: call DispatchIndexedFunction(col, 0x100, 0) and increment row by stride
   - Increment column by dwColStride and continue
8. Move to next dimension parameter set and decrement loop counter
9. Return after processing all 4 dimensions

Parameters:
pArrayDescriptor (int) - Pointer to array descriptor structure containing base array address and bounds

Returns:
void - Function modifies external state through DispatchIndexedFunction calls

Special Cases:
- Function checks flag bits (& 1) to determine if elements are active/inactive
- Uses nested array element structure indicating multi-dimensional indexing
- Bounds checking prevents access outside array limits
- Processes in fixed 4-iteration loop pattern

functions.name: ProcessInventorySlotRange
functions.comment:
Iterates through linked list of inventory slots and processes coordinate ranges for active slots.

Algorithm:
1. Load inventory panel structure pointer from ECX parameter
2. Load slot table base address from panel offset +0x38
3. Get first slot pointer from table offset +0x64
4. Enter loop: check if current slot is active (byte at +0xc, bit 0 set)
5. If active: call GetDirectionSlotIndex to determine direction slot index
6. Call ProcessCoordinateRangeWithFlags for slot primary bounds (panel offset +0x18)
7. Call ProcessCoordinateRangeWithFlags for slot secondary bounds (panel offset +0x2c)
8. Advance to next slot: load pointer from current slot at offset +0x10
9. Continue loop until next pointer equals table base (end of linked list)
10. Return void

Parameters:
  pInventoryPanel (void*) - Inventory/panel structure pointer; contains:
    offset +0x38: pSlotTable (void*) - pointer to slot table base
    slot table +0x64: first slot pointer
    offset +0xe from first load: pSlotTableStart (void*)

Returns:
  void - Modifies slot coordinate ranges in-place via ProcessCoordinateRangeWithFlags

Special Cases:
  - Inventory panel is passed in ECX register (fastcall convention)
  - Slot table uses circular linked list: next pointer comparison determines end
  - Only processes slots with active flag bit (0x01) set at offset +0xc
  - Direction calculation uses NEG/SBB pattern (convert byte to 0/-1, AND with 0x2)
  - Slot offset +0x3 used for flag byte extraction

Magic Numbers:
  0x0c - Offset to slot flags byte (0x01 = active bit)
  0x03 - Byte offset within slot for flag check
  0x10 - Offset to next slot pointer within slot structure  
  0x18 - Offset in panel to coordinate range structure 1
  0x2c - Offset in panel to coordinate range structure 2
  0x38 - Offset in panel to slot table pointer
  0x64 - Offset in slot table to first slot pointer
  0x02 - Bitmask for direction parameter calculation
  0x0e - Offset to slot table base within first loaded dword

functions.name: RenderDiagonalLinePattern
functions.comment:
Renders diagonal line pattern with interpolated graphics.

Algorithm:
1. Extract character tier from property offset +0x4
2. Load property root pointer from offset +0x38
3. Get linked segment array base from pointer at offset +100
4. For each segment in array: compare coordinates to compute deltas
5. Calculate absolute delta X and Y values for distance calculations
6. Load rendering mode and lookup graphics ID from classification table
7. If segment active flag clear: step through coordinates and render intermediate points
8. Render corner/edge graphics based on tier mode and coordinate relationships
9. Load final segment value from lookup table using classification
10. Advance to next linked segment; repeat until reaching array termination
11. Call ProcessArrayElementFlags to finalize state and return

Parameters:
nLineProperties (int) - Configuration handle containing tier lookup and grid segment pointers

Returns:
void - Updates global rendering state and display buffers

Special Cases:
Segment type determines graphics lookup table (case 0=corner, 1=edge, 3=diagonal). Flag 0x02 determines stride multiplier. Tier 0x11 uses different graphics set. List termination when pCurrentPoint equals root array pointer.

functions.name: SetPlayerSlotErrorState
functions.comment:
Initialize player slot error state and sync error information from Storm.dll

Algorithm:
1. Load current slot index from unit offset 0x1ec
2. Check if slot error field (0x138 + index*4) equals -1
3. If not -1, mark slot status field (0xfc + index*4) as 0xffffffff error flag
4. Call Ordinal_10010 with Storm error parameter at offset 0x1f0
5. Extract error code from returned pointer offset +0xc into slot array
6. Extract additional field from returned pointer offset +0x10 into slot array
7. Return 1 to indicate success

Parameters:
pUnit (UnitAny*): Pointer to unit structure containing slot array and error tracking fields

Returns:
1 (success, always)

Special Cases:
If error field pre-set to 0xffffffff, status field update is skipped to avoid redundancy

functions.name: RotateState
functions.comment:
Rotate state value within valid range (0-3) and synchronize related state fields.

Algorithm:
1. Load current state index from pStateArray[0x7b]
2. If state field at [index + 0x4e] is uninitialized (0xFFFFFFFF):
   a. Generate random seed value via Ordinal_10917 (Storm.dll RandSeed)
   b. Store lowest 2 bits (mask 0x3) in state field [index + 0x4e]
   c. Mirror value to backup field [index + 0x3f]
   d. Proceed to step 3
3. Else, calculate next cyclic state:
   a. Increment previous state from [index + 0x3f] by 1
   b. Apply mask 0x80000003 (preserve sign bit and low 2 bits)
   c. Perform sign extension if result is negative (convert to positive mod 4)
   d. Compare calculated state to current [index + 0x4e]
   e. If equal, return 0 (no state change needed)
   f. Update [index + 0x3f] with new state value
4. Invoke FUN_6fd91dd0 to update related data structures
5. Return 1 (state changed)

Parameters:
pStateArray (dword*): Pointer to state structure array, offsets: [0x7b]=index, [0x3e]=table ptr, [0x3f]=prev state, [0x4e]=curr state

Returns:
1 - State was rotated and updated
0 - State unchanged (cyclic check failed)

Special Cases:
- Uninitialized state (-1) triggers random seed generation via Storm.dll RandSeed (Ordinal_10917)
- Wraparound at 4 returns to 0 (modulo 4 arithmetic)
- Sign extension handles negative intermediate values

Magic Numbers:
0x7b (123) - State index field offset
0x3e (62) - Table pointer field offset  
0x3f (63) - Previous state field offset
0x4e (78) - Current state field offset
0x4 (4) - State field size in bytes, scale factor for array indexing
0x10 (16) - Structure size for table entries
0x3 (3) - Modulo 4 mask (0-3 valid range)
0x80000003 - Mask: preserve sign (0x80000000) and low 2 bits (0x3)
0xFFFFFFFF (-1) - Uninitialized state sentinel
0xFFFFFFFFC (-4) - Mask for sign extension in negative values

Ordinals:
Ordinal_10917 - Storm.dll RandSeed, generates random number for state initialization

functions.name: ComputeDirectionalCoordinates
functions.signature: void ComputeDirectionalCoordinates(int * pSourceCoords, int * pDestCoords, int nDirection, int nOffsetType)
functions.comment:
Compute directional offset coordinates based on direction and offset type parameters.

Algorithm:
1. Load direction selector from stack [ESP + 0x4]
2. Branch on direction value (0-3) using jump table at 0x6fd91eb4
3. For each direction:
   - Copy source coordinate fields to destination
   - Apply directional transformations (add/subtract offsets from source)
   - If nOffsetType == 1: Apply 0x10 (16 pixel) adjustment
   - If nOffsetType == 2: Apply 0x8 (8 pixel) adjustment
   - If nOffsetType == 3: Apply 0x8 adjustment (direction 3 only)
4. Return with stack cleanup (RET 0x8)

Parameters:
- pSourceCoords (ECX): Pointer to source 4-DWORD structure [x, y, width, height]
- pDestCoords (EDX): Pointer to destination 4-DWORD structure for computed coords
- dwDirection (Stack +0x4): Direction selector (0=UP/left, 1=DOWN/right, 2=RIGHT, 3=LEFT)
- nOffsetType (Stack +0x8): Offset adjustment type (0=none, 1=large, 2=small, 3=small)

Returns: void (result in pDestCoords)

Special Cases:
- Invalid direction (>3): Falls through to end without modification
- Direction 3 with nOffsetType==3: Applies +0x8 adjustment
- nOffsetType != 1,2,3: No adjustment applied after compute

functions.name: IncrementAndApplyRotation
functions.comment:
Increment and apply rotation/directional state to unit animation

Algorithm:
1. Load rotation slot index from unit data offset 0x7b
2. Check if current rotation is uninitialized (0xffffffff)
   - If uninitialized: Call Ordinal_10917 to get initial rotation, mask to 3-bit value (0-7), store at offset 0x4e and 0x3f
   - If initialized: Increment current rotation (offset 0x3f) cyclically within 8 directions (modulo 8)
3. Validate cycled rotation differs from stored rotation (offset 0x4e), return 0 if identical (no change)
4. Store new rotation value at offset 0x3f
5. Call FUN_6fd91f70 to apply rotation to affected unit animation data
6. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
  pUnitData - Pointer to unit structure containing rotation state at offsets 0x7b (slot), 0x3f (current rotation), 0x4e (stored rotation), 0xf8 (config table), 0x3e (indirect index table)

Returns:
  1 - Rotation applied successfully
  0 - No rotation change needed (current == next)

Special Cases:
  - Uninitialized rotation (0xffffffff) triggers Ordinal_10917 call to seed initial value
  - Rotation values constrained to 3-bit range [0-7] for 8-directional animation
  - Cyclic increment uses signed modulo arithmetic: (value + 1) & 0x80000007 with sign adjustment

Magic Numbers:
  0x7b - Offset to rotation slot index (8 bits)
  0x3f - Offset to current rotation state (8 bits)
  0x4e - Offset to stored rotation state (8 bits)
  0x3e - Offset to config/lookup table pointer
  0xf8 - Offset to indirect table pointer
  0xffffffff - Uninitialized marker for rotation state
  0x7 - Mask for 3-bit rotation value (7 directions max)
  0x80000007 - Signed modulo 8 mask (for cyclic increment)

Structure Layout:
  Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
  0x3e   | 4    | ConfigPtr  | dword* | Points to configuration lookup table
  0x3f   | 1    | CurRotation | byte | Current rotation index (0-7)
  0x4e   | 1    | StoredRotation | byte | Last applied rotation index
  0x7b   | 1    | SlotIndex  | byte | Active rotation slot number
  0xf8   | 4    | TablePtr   | dword* | Animation effect lookup table

functions.name: CalculatePanelPosition
functions.signature: void CalculatePanelPosition(int * pSourceRect, int * pDestRect, uint dwAlignment, int nAdjustOffset)
functions.comment:
Calculate panel position based on alignment mode and optional offset adjustment

Algorithm:
1. Load nAlignment parameter (0-7) to determine alignment case
2. Copy source rectangle [0] and [1] to destination [0] and [1]
3. Apply alignment-specific transformations:
   - Case 0: dest[1] = src[3] + src[1] (top offset + top)
   - Case 1: Adjust for centered mode if bAdjustOffset=1: dest[0] += src[2]/2 + 8
   - Case 2: dest[0] = src[0] - dest[2] (right-align)
   - Case 3: Adjust for centered if bAdjustOffset=1
   - Case 4: dest[1] = src[1] - dest[3] (bottom-align)
   - Case 5: Similar to case 4 with center adjustment
   - Case 6: dest[0] = src[2] + src[0] (width + left)
   - Case 7: Combined offset calculation
4. If bAdjustOffset=1 and alignment requires, apply adjustment: offset/2 ± 8

Parameters:
  int *pSourceRect - Source rectangle: [0]=X, [1]=Y, [2]=Width, [3]=Height offset
  int *pDestRect - Destination rectangle to populate
  uint nAlignment - Alignment mode (0-7): 0=Top, 1=TopCenter, 2=Right, 3=RightCenter, 4=Bottom, 5=BottomCenter, 6=WidthOffset, 7=CombinedOffset
  int bAdjustOffset - Boolean flag (1=apply offset adjustment, 0=none)

Returns:
  void - Modifies pDestRect in place

Special Cases:
  - Case 1,3,5,7 with bAdjustOffset=0: fall through to default behavior
  - Center adjustment divides dest[2] or dest[3] by 2 using arithmetic shift
  - Magic constant 0x8 (8) added after division adjustment
  - Each case operates on different panel edge alignment

Magic Numbers:
  0x7 - Max alignment mode value (0-7 valid)
  0x1 - bAdjustOffset flag value
  0x8 - Offset constant added to center adjustments
  0xc - Offset for height field (dest[3])
  0x8 - Offset for width field (dest[2])

Structure Layout (Rectangle):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
     0 |    4 | x          | int  | X coordinate
     4 |    4 | y          | int  | Y coordinate
     8 |    4 | width      | int  | Width value
     c |    4 | height     | int  | Height value

functions.name: UpdateUnitDirectionalAnimation
functions.comment:
Update unit directional animation frame based on position and movement state.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve unit's current directional state from offset +0x4e
2. If directional state uninitialized (0xffffffff):
   a. Initialize directional state with random value (Ordinal_10917) masked to 0-3
   b. Store in unit offset +0x4e and backup at +0x3f
   c. Initialize animation frame (offset +0x6c) with random bit masked to 0-1
   d. Load the frame value into uVar4
3. Else (directional state already initialized):
   a. Compute new direction from current position (+0x5d) and facing (+0x3f), modulo 4
   b. Compute new frame from position+1, modulo 2
   c. If both direction AND frame unchanged, return 0 (no change)
   d. Otherwise update facing direction (+0x3f) and continue
4. Store computed frame value into unit offset +0x5d
5. Retrieve animation table pointer from offset +0xf8
6. Load unit animation table index from offset +0x3e
7. If frame == 1: Call ComputeDirectionalCoordinates (special animation)
8. Else: Call FUN_6fd92200 (default animation)
9. Return 1 (animation updated)

Parameters:
pUnit (UnitAny*): Pointer to unit structure with animation state (offsets: +0x3e=anim_table_idx, +0x3f=facing_dir, +0x4e=direction, +0x5d=frame, +0x6c=animation_frame, +0xf8=animation_table, +0x1ec=unit_id/index)

Returns:
int: 1 if animation updated, 0 if no change needed

Special Cases:
- First call initializes random direction and frame
- Modulo arithmetic handles wraparound at direction=4, frame=2
- Negative modulo handled via arithmetic: (v-1)|mask)+1 pattern for signed modulo
- Two code paths: ComputeDirectionalCoordinates (frame=1) vs FUN_6fd92200 (frame!=1)

functions.name: TransformCoordinates
functions.signature: void TransformCoordinates(int * pSourceCoords, int * pDestCoords, dword nMode, int nAdjustmentFlag)
functions.comment:
Transform screen/viewport coordinates based on direction and adjustment mode.

Algorithm:
1. Load adjustment flag from stack parameter 4
2. Validate transform mode (0-3) using bounds check; fail if >= 4
3. Switch on transform mode to select calculation branch
4. For each mode:
   - Load source and destination coordinate fields
   - Compute offset deltas (source - dest adjustments)
   - Write results to destination coordinates
   - If adjustment flag == 1: apply +0x10 or -0x10 offset
   - If adjustment flag == 2: apply +/-0x08 offset
   - If adjustment flag == 3: apply -0x08 offset (mode 3 only)

Parameters:
  pSourceCoords (int*): Source coordinate structure array with fields [x, y, offsetX, offsetY]
  pDestCoords (int*): Destination coordinate structure array, modified with transformed values
  nMode (dword): Transform direction (0=bottom, 1=left, 2=top, 3=right) - validates 0-3
  nAdjustmentFlag (int): Optional adjustment offset modifier (0=none, 1=+/-0x10, 2=+/-0x08, 3=-0x08 for mode 3)

Returns: void

Magic Numbers:
  0x10 (16): Standard offset adjustment magnitude for modes 0, 1, 2, 3
  0x08 (8): Half-offset adjustment for modes 1, 3 with flags 2/3
  0x3: Maximum valid transform mode value

Related Functions:
- Called by coordinate processing routines for screen transform operations
- Dependencies: Array index arithmetic on 32-bit fields

functions.name: UpdateEntityDirectionalMovement
functions.comment:
Updates entity directional movement state or initializes it on first call.

Algorithm:
1. Load entity slot index from pEntity[0x7b]
2. If direction state uninitialized (field 0x4e == 0xffffffff):
   a. Generate random direction: call Ordinal_10917 (RandSeed), mask to 0-3
   b. Store direction in slot field 0x4e and backup in field 0x3f
   c. Generate random movement: call Ordinal_10917, mask to 0-1
   d. Store movement state in field 0x6c, load as dwMovementState
3. Else (already initialized):
   a. Calculate next direction = (previous + current direction) & 0x80000003 (modulo 4)
   b. Normalize negative values using two's complement adjustment
   c. Calculate next movement = (previous + 1) & 0x80000001 (modulo 2)
   d. If both equal current values, return 0 (no change needed)
   e. Update current direction field 0x3f with next direction
4. Store movement state in field 0x5d
5. Update animation state fields based on direction bit:
   a. Field calculation: (direction & 0x1) selects between 0x60 and 0x38 (animation IDs)
   b. Write to fields at (index+1)*4 and index*4+5 offsets
6. Fetch coordinate transformation base: iVar1 = pEntity[0x3e][8 + index*16]
7. Branch on movement state:
   a. If movement==1: call ComputeDirectionalCoordinates (linear movement)
   b. Else: call FUN_6fd92200 (alternative movement logic)
8. Return 1 (state changed)

Parameters:
- pEntity (uint *): IMPLICIT ECX. Pointer to entity structure. Contains:
  - Offset 0x1ec (0x7b*4): Current slot/activity index
  - Offset 0x138 (0x4e*4): Current direction state (0-3), 0xffffffff if uninitialized
  - Offset 0xfc (0x3f*4): Previous direction
  - Offset 0x1b0 (0x6c*4): Current movement state (0-1)
  - Offset 0x174 (0x5d*4): Movement sequence
  - Offset 0xf8 (0x3e*4): Coordinate/geometry table pointer

Returns:
- 0: State unchanged (already calculated for current parameters)
- 1: State changed (animation/movement updated or initialized)

functions.name: UpdateDirectionalState
functions.comment:
Update directional state based on current slot orientation.

Algorithm:
1. Load current slot index from pUnitState[0x7b]
2. Check if slot orientation is uninitialized (0xffffffff)
3. If uninitialized: Call Ordinal_10917 to get orientation, store as (value & 1) + 1
4. If initialized: Calculate expected state (2 or 1 based on previous state != 1)
5. Compare expected with current: if equal, return early (no change needed)
6. Update state fields at slot offsets +0x3f and +0x4e
7. Load table offset from pUnitState[0x3e] and index for current slot
8. If state == 1: Call ComputeDirectionalCoordinates with direction=1, speed=0
9. If state != 1: Call FUN_6fd92200 with direction=(state), speed=0
10. Return success (1)

Parameters:
pUnitState (uint *) - Pointer to unit state structure containing:
  [0x7b] - Current active slot index
  [0x3e] - Pointer to coordinate/direction table (offset base)
  [slot * 4 + 0xfc] - Current directional state (1 or 2)
  [slot * 4 + 0x3f] - Expected directional state field
  [slot * 4 + 0x138] - Orientation state field (-1 = uninitialized)

Returns:
0 - No state change needed (early exit when state matches expected)
1 - Successfully updated directional state

Special Cases:
- Uninitialized orientation (-1) triggers randomization via Ordinal_10917
- State encoding: 1 = direction1, 2 = direction2
- Table offset calculation uses slot_index * 4 bytes per entry

Magic Numbers:
0x1ec (492) - Slot index field offset in state struct
0x138 (312) - Orientation state array offset
0xfc (252) - Directional state array offset
0x3f (63) - Expected state field offset within slot entry
0x4e (78) - Current orientation field offset within slot entry
0x3e (62) - Coordinate table base pointer offset
0xffffffff - Uninitialized orientation sentinel
0x1 - Direction bit mask for Ordinal_10917 result
0x10 - Bytes per table entry (slot * 4 to dword offset)

functions.name: UpdatePanelSlotDisplay
functions.comment:
Updates the panel slot display index and recalculates panel position.

Algorithm:
1. Get current panel slot index from pPanelData[0x7b]
2. If slot display state at [slot + 0x4e] is uninitialized (-1):
   a. Call Ordinal_10917 (Storm.DLL - random seed) to get random value
   b. Store lower 3 bits in display state [slot + 0x4e]
   c. Copy display state to previous state [slot + 0x3f]
   d. Skip to recalculate position
3. Otherwise, calculate next slot incrementally:
   a. Increment previous state [slot + 0x3f], mask to 3-bit signed cyclic (0x80000007)
   b. Apply signed modulo-8 arithmetic if result negative
   c. If calculated slot equals display state, return 0 (no change)
   d. Update previous state with calculated value
4. Recalculate panel position via CalculatePanelPosition
5. Return 1 (update successful)

Parameters:
pPanelData (dword *): Pointer to panel data structure
  - [0x7b]: Current slot index (32-bit offset)
  - [slot + 0x3f]: Previous display state (3-bit value)
  - [slot + 0x4e]: Current display state (3-bit value, -1 if uninitialized)
  - [0x3e]: Configuration table base
  - [0xf8]: Secondary table base

Returns:
1 - Panel position recalculated and updated
0 - No slot state change (previous equals current display state)

Special Cases:
- First call with uninitialized state (-1): Uses random initialization
- Cyclic slot transitions: Values wrap using modulo-8 signed arithmetic
- Magic number 0x80000007: Cyclic mask for 3-bit signed values (range -4 to 3)
- Slot width: 0x10 bytes per slot in configuration table

Related Functions:
- Ordinal_10917: Storm.DLL random seed generation
- CalculatePanelPosition: Updates UI position based on slot index

functions.name: ProcessCoordinateTransformation
functions.comment: Setting prototype: int __fastcall ProcessCoordinateTransformation(uint *pUnit)

functions.name: ProcessPlayerSlotState
functions.comment:
Processes player slot state initialization based on slot type.

Algorithm:
1. Switch on bySlotType (0x00-0x04)
2. Type 0x00: Initialize error slots - Call FUN_6fd92d20 twice with different config pointers (0x6fde0da8, 0x6fde0e98) and handler labels (0x6fd929b0, 0x6fd92a90), then call FUN_6fd93110(param_1, 1, 0x11)
3. Type 0x01: Initialize inventory slots - Call FUN_6fd92d20 twice with config (0x6fde0f88, 0x6fde1078) and handlers (0x6fd92b40, 0x6fd92ba0), then FUN_6fd93110(param_1, 0x28, 0x2e)
4. Type 0x02: Configure viewport slot (0x4b-0x53) - Call FindNodeByState(0x4b), Ordinal_10010(0x4b) to get state data, copy 4 dwords from offsets 0xc,0x10,0x4,0x8 into viewport buffer, call FUN_6fd931e0 for layout, load center coord (height/2 via CDQ+SAR), loop viewport subslots 0x4f-0x53 calling Ordinal_10010, calculate coordinate offsets via division, store dimensions 0x20-0x2c in node
5. Type 0x03: Initialize transmutation panel (0x67-0x6a) - Call FUN_6fd92d20 twice for config (0x6fde1168, 0x6fde1258), call FindNodeByState(0x68), OR node[0x38] with g_dwTransformModeFlag, call FUN_6fd93110(param_1, 0x67, 0x6a)
6. Type 0x04: Initialize minion slots - Process two ranges: 0x6f-0x70 and 0x6e-0x6f with nested distance checks, call SetSlotValue with -1/-1 to disable overlapping minions, call FUN_6fd93090 and FUN_6fd93110 for each range
7. Return void

Parameters:
pUnitNode: int * - Pointer to unit/player data structure containing slot information
bySlotType: byte - Slot category selector (0=error, 1=inventory, 2=viewport, 3=transmutation, 4=minions)

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
- Type 0x02: CDQ+SAR sequence at 0x6fd927c9 performs arithmetic right shift for signed division by 2
- Type 0x04: Nested loop with distance check (CheckPointsWithinDistance) determines minion collision
- Type 0x03: g_dwTransformModeFlag is global at 0x6fe04648, OR'd into slot state
- Type 0x00/0x01: Use FUN_6fd92d20 which appears to bind handlers to slot callbacks

Magic Numbers:
0x4b: Viewport slot ID
0x4f: First viewport subslot (range 0x4f-0x53, 5 elements)
0x53: Last viewport subslot
0x6f: Minion type 1 start
0x70: Minion type 1 end
0x6e: Minion type 2 start
0x6d-0x6a: Transmutation panel range
0x80: Jump table threshold (5 cases)

functions.name: ProcessPlayerSlotFiltering
functions.signature: void ProcessPlayerSlotFiltering(int * pSlotState, int * pSlotList, dword * pfnFilterInclude, dword * pfnFilterExclude)
functions.comment:
Filters active player slot states using callback predicates and maintains linked list relationships.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 4 temporary filter arrays (local_44, local_80, local_bc, local_f8) with sentinel values (0xFFFFFFFF/-1)
2. Copy initial slot pointers from pSlotState[5] and pSlotState[6] to output buffer
3. Load all active slot state IDs from pSlotList[1+] via Ordinal_10010 lookup, storing fields at +4 and +8 offsets
4. Filter phase: iterate pSlotList entries, call pfnFilterInclude/pfnFilterExclude callbacks
   - If pfnFilterInclude returns false OR callback NULL: mark slot as excluded (set arrays to 0xFFFFFFFF), decrement counter
   - Else if pfnFilterInclude NULL or returns true: mark slot as included, increment counter
5. Second pass: for each active slot, call FindNodeByState to retrieve container node
   - Copy 4 state value fields (offset +0x20) from filtered slot data
   - Special handling for state type 0x02: set field at offset +0x38+4 based on value type (0x01 or 0x28)
   - Special handling for state type 0x06: call Ordinal_10917 to get random bit, set field based on slot value (1/3)
6. Call pfnFilterExclude callback if provided
7. Link slot relationships via GetOrCreateLinkedListNode/SetSlotValue unless pSlotState[4] == 0x04 (skip linking)

Parameters:
  pSlotState - Pointer to slot state container array (offset +4/+8 for pointers, +0x10 for mode byte at +4)
  pSlotList - Active player slot list (entry 1+ contains slot IDs, entries are 4 dwords apart)
  pfnFilterInclude - Optional callback returning non-zero to include slot, NULL means all pass
  pfnFilterExclude - Optional callback invoked after processing each slot

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Ordinal_10010(slotId) returns slot descriptor with fields at +4 (prev ptr) and +8 (next ptr)
  - Ordinal_10917(ptr) returns RNG bit masked with 0x01
  - State ID 0x1b is treated as special "previous state" target
  - 0xFFFFFFFF marks excluded/uninitialized slot entries throughout
  - Array indices stored as 0xFFFFFFFF when slot filtered out
  
Note: Function uses 4 stack-allocated temporary arrays optimized away (local_1e0, local_1e4, local_1f0, local_1f8)

functions.name: ProcessSlotProximityChecks
functions.signature: void ProcessSlotProximityChecks(int * pSlotList, int nStateIdStart, int nStateIdEnd)
functions.comment:
Iterates through state IDs and checks proximity between nodes, updating slots based on distance checks.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize outer loop with starting state ID (param_2)
2. If starting state ID <= ending state ID:
   a. Find node matching current state ID
   b. Create or retrieve linked list node for state ID
   c. Initialize inner loop with starting state ID
   d. For each inner state ID from start to end:
      - If inner state ID != outer state ID:
        * Find node matching inner state ID
        * Check if points at offset 0x20 are within distance (-1 = unlimited)
        * If proximity check returns non-zero (points within distance):
          - Call SetSlotValue to mark slot with 0xffffffff and -1
      - Increment inner state ID
   e. Increment outer state ID
3. Return void

Parameters:
- pSlotList (int *): Pointer to list/map of slots, passed in ECX (fastcall)
- nStateIdStart (int): Starting state ID value, passed in EDX (fastcall)
- nStateIdEnd (int): Ending state ID value (inclusive), passed on stack

Returns:
- void: No return value

Special Cases:
- Points stored at offset +0x20 from container (coordinate data)
- Distance check uses -1 parameter (likely means unlimited range)
- Skips comparison when state IDs are identical (dwStateId != dwStateId_00)
- SetSlotValue parameters: 0xffffffff (value), -1 (flags)

functions.name: ProcessLinkedListNodeRange
functions.signature: void ProcessLinkedListNodeRange(int * pNodeList, int nStartIdx, int nEndIdx)
functions.comment:
Iterate over linked list node range and process active unit nodes.

Algorithm:
1. Validate range: if (nStartIdx > nEndIdx) exit early
2. Outer loop: iterate nCurrentIdx from nStartIdx to nEndIdx
3. Find node state using FindNodeByState() and check if state equals 3 (active)
4. If active: locate unit using FindUnitInActiveList(), find linked node via FindLinkedListNodeByValue()
5. Calculate field offset: iNodeOffset = piLinkedNode - pUnitNode
6. Inner loop: process 8 unit sub-fields (unit->field_0 through unit->field_1c, 4-byte stride)
7. For each field: check if field != 0 AND offset_field == -1 (indicating empty slot)
8. If condition met: retrieve parent state, call CompareCoordinates(), insert node via InsertLinkedListNode()
9. Advance to next field: pUnitNode += 4 bytes
10. Loop back: nLoopCount-- until exhausted

Parameters:
- pNodeList (IMPLICIT ECX): base pointer to node list/state array
- nStartIdx (IMPLICIT EDX): starting index for iteration range
- nEndIdx (Stack[0x4]): ending index for iteration range (inclusive)

Returns:
- void (result in EAX unused)

Special Cases:
- Uses __d2call convention (EBX saved, result in EAX ignored)
- Field offset calculation allows sparse access patterns
- Inner loop unrolled: processes 8 iterations fixed
- Magic number 0x264: offset within parent structure for linked list head
- Magic number 0x20: coordinate data field offset within node

Related Functions:
- FindNodeByState() - locate state descriptor
- FindUnitInActiveList() - find active unit by index
- FindLinkedListNodeByValue() - find linked node matching criteria
- CompareCoordinates() - coordinate comparison logic
- InsertLinkedListNode() - insert node into linked list

functions.name: ProcessIsometricViewTiles
functions.comment:
Processes isometric view tile rendering data from room geometry, calculating visibility and pathfinding information.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate isometric viewport data buffer via Ordinal_10010 (0x4c bytes for spatial metadata)
2. Extract room dimension parameters: width (iVar18), height (iVar19), viewport offsets from param_1[8..9]
3. Calculate grid division size: divide room dimensions by 32-byte cell size using arithmetic shift (SAR 0x5)
4. Initialize local_e0 array (42 dwords) to zero for node bounding boxes
5. Call FUN_6fd94260 to populate initial coordinate data from room viewport parameters
6. Process up to 3 isometric node types (uVar23 loop: 1, 2, 3):
   a. Retrieve node pointer from Ordinal_10918 for current node type
   b. Call FUN_6fd94260 to compute node boundary coordinates relative to viewport
   c. Compare node rectangle with existing processed nodes via CompareRectanglesWithinThreshold
   d. Update min/max viewport bounds (local_f4, local_f0, local_130) as nodes processed
   e. Validate bounds divisible by 32: if width or height not aligned, log assertion via Ordinal_10025
7. Calculate final grid dimensions: round-up division and add padding (+2):
   local_134 = ceil(Y_extent / 32) + 2 (grid height)
   iVar18 = ceil(X_extent / 32) + 2 (grid width)
8. Allocate 4 grids via Ordinal_10045 (grid IDs 0x63b-0x63e):
   puVar7: Node ownership grid (1-3 for node type)
   puVar8: Movement cost/pheromone grid
   puVar9: Visibility/line-of-sight flags (0x00/0x01/0x02)
   puVar10: Adjacency/direction flags (0x01/0x02/0x04/0x08/0x10/0x20/0x40/0x80)
9. Zero-initialize all 4 grids (STOSD.REP pattern clear)
10. For each node type 0-2:
    a. Calculate grid offset from viewport bounds (local_a8 node array entries)
    b. Retrieve node orientation via Ordinal_10917
    c. Mark grid cells: set puVar7[cell] = node type ID + 1
    d. Clear cost/visibility for cells under node footprint
    e. Extract sub-nodes from node container (auStack_d0 offsets):
        - Switch on node sub-type (0x10 byte offset determines orientation):
          case 0: Mark at (X, Y)
          case 1: Mark at (X, Y+4)
          case 2: Mark at (X+1, Y+4)
          case 3: Mark at (X, Y+2)
          case 4: Mark at (X+1, Y+2)
    f. Path corridor traversal: create diagonal pathfinding corridors with decreasing cost
       - For each column, test accessibility via Ordinal_10918
       - Toggle orientation based on blocked cells
       - Mark cells 0x02 for corridor obstacles, accumulate cost/counter
11. Build adjacency graph:
    a. For each grid cell, analyze 4 neighbors (N/S/E/W):
       - Check cell ownership, compare node IDs, verify cost thresholds
       - Set direction flags 0x08/0x04/0x02/0x01 (N/S/E/W) if connected
    b. Check cost-based adjacency (puVar8 variance == 1 indicates adjacent costs)
    c. Validate diagonal adjacency against obstruction grid (puVar9 == 2)
    d. Set compound direction flags (0x80/0x40/0x20/0x10) for secondary connections
12. Final grid pass:
    a. For each cell, map Preset IDs from direction flags to actual preset values
    b. Check flags 0x10/0x20/0x40/0x80 -> lookup in DAT_6fde1780-178c arrays using cell value>>4
    c. If preset ID == 0, log error via Ordinal_10025 (0x76f or 0x77c)
    d. Write final preset ID back to cell
13. Accumulate viewport statistics:
    a. For each node, copy mapped preset values into adjacent array buffers
    b. Count cells with preset > 0x23e, increment auStack_d0+6 counter (stats)
14. Sort node type array (local_a8[0-27]) by grid offset using bubble sort if needed
15. For each node type 0-2:
    a. Call FindNodeByState(pdwUnitNode, type_ID + 0x4c) to get node entity
    b. Write grid statistics to node structure offsets:
       +0x20/0x24/0x28/0x2c: grid offsets for visibility quad
       +0x214/0x218: adjacency counts
16. Release allocated grids via Ordinal_10046 (IDs 0x7b5-0x7b8)
17. Return EAX containing processed node entity pointer

Parameters:
param_1: UnitAny * - Pointer to unit/room node containing viewport geometry
  - [0]: *pNodePtr (points to first sub-node)
  - [+0x14]: Node child list base address
  - [+0x20/0x24]: Viewport offset Y/X in pixels
  - [+0x4c/0x50/0x54/0x58]: Room dimensions (width/height/bottom/right in tiles)

Returns:
EAX: UnitAny * - Pointer to processed node entity (from FindNodeByState)

Special Cases:
- If node count > 3, assertion logged via Ordinal_10025 at 0x621
- If grid width not divisible by 32, assertion at 0x630
- If grid height not divisible by 32, assertion at 0x631
- If preset lookup fails (value == 0x00), assertion at 0x76f or 0x77c
- Phantom variables (optimized away): auStack_90[22], auStack_d0[6], local_b8[3]
- Function uses stack allocation for 4 local grid buffers and temporary coefficient arrays

functions.name: CalcDirectionalOffsets
functions.signature: void CalcDirectionalOffsets(int * pBaseCoords, int * pOutputCoords, int nDirection, int nStepX, int nStepY)
functions.comment:
Calculates X and Y offset deltas based on direction code using trigonometric approximations.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize nOffsetX and nOffsetY to zero
2. Switch on nDirection code (0-5):
   - 0: North (up) - X=0, Y=-nStepY
   - 1: NE diagonal - X=-nStepX, Y=truncate(nStepY*0.5)
   - 2: SE diagonal - X=nStepX, Y=truncate(nStepY*0.5)
   - 3,4: SW/NW diagonals - Y=±nStepX, X=truncate(-nStepY*2/3)
   - Default: Return zero offsets
3. Normalize result by subtracting sign extension bits
4. Store calculated offsets at pOutputCoords[1] and pOutputCoords[0]
5. Copy nStepX to pOutputCoords[2], nStepY to pOutputCoords[3], nDirection to pOutputCoords[4]

Parameters:
- pBaseCoords: Pointer to base X,Y coordinates [X at +0, Y at +4]
- pOutputCoords: Pointer to output result array (5 elements: nNewX, nNewY, nStepX, nStepY, nDirection)
- nDirection: Direction code (0=North, 1=NE, 2=SE, 3=SW, 4=NW, 5+=invalid)
- nStepX: X step magnitude for horizontal movement
- nStepY: Y step magnitude for vertical movement

Returns:
- void; stores result at pOutputCoords array (5 dword elements)

Special Cases:
- Direction 0: Pure vertical (up), no X component
- Diagonal directions (1-4) use fixed-point approximation for 45-degree angles
- Invalid direction (>4) defaults to zero offset, pBaseCoords copied unchanged
- All offsets negated based on direction quadrant

functions.name: RenderAndProcessGameGrid
functions.comment:
Render and process a 2D game grid structure with multiple data layers and tile rendering.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve grid configuration and unit data references from input structure
2. Extract grid dimensions (rows, columns) and flags from parameter structure offsets
3. Initialize three parallel grid data layers (InitializeGridStructure x3) for different grid types
4. Populate all 64 grid cells (8x8) with indexed function dispatch calls using flag 0x40002
5. If tier index equals zero, render grid with Bresenham line algorithm for rasterization
6. Clear the grid array pointers buffer (set 15 elements to null, retaining first 2)
7. Setup array pointers to grid config, base data, and two derived grid layers
8. If grid flag type is non-zero, load character stat at offset 0x28 and process grid data via FUN_6fd9afe0
9. If grid flag mask is non-zero, load character stat at offset 0x2c and process grid data via FUN_6fd9afe0
10. Load three values from grid data layer at offsets 0x64, 0x68, 0x6c and process via FUN_6fd9afe0
11. Switch on grid config type value (offset +8) to set render flags (0x100, 0x120000, 0x100000, 0xa00000, 0x1600000)
12. For each grid cell, check if element bits 0x3f0ff80 are clear and dispatch indexed function with render flags
13. Finalize by processing collection flags on both grid data layers with parameter 0

Parameters:
  pGridConfig (int *): Pointer to grid configuration structure, contains: [0]=grid base ptr, [4]=column count-1, [8]=pointer to grid data, [c]=row count-1, [10]=column count-1, [14]=flags (bits: [17:16]=type, [15:12]=mask)

Returns:
  void - No return value, function processes grid in-place via pointers in structure

Special Cases:
  - Tier index zero triggers additional Bresenham line rendering (DDA line rasterization)
  - Grid flag type and mask values trigger conditional stat loading at different offsets
  - Switch statement case 0x1f contains conditional test on tier value (offset +4) for value 0x75
  - Cell element filtering uses inverted mask (0x3f0ff80) to skip occupied cells

Magic Numbers:
  0x40002: Standard grid dispatch function flag
  0x3f0ff80: Cell occupancy mask (used inverted to detect empty cells)
  0x100, 0x120000, 0x100000, 0xa00000, 0x1600000: Grid rendering mode flags
  0x28, 0x2c: Character stat offsets within unit data
  0x64, 0x68, 0x6c: Grid data array field offsets
  0x75: Character class/type comparison value

functions.name: AllocateAndRegisterGameTile
functions.signature: int * AllocateAndRegisterGameTile(int nListHead, int nMinX, int nMinY, int nMaxX, int nMaxY, uint dwFlags, uint dwExtraData1, uint dwExtraData2, int nIndex)
functions.comment:
Allocate and register a game grid tile with rendering properties.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate and initialize new unit data structure via AllocateAndInitializeUnitData()
2. Set tile bounding box coordinates: min/max X and Y in unit structure
3. Insert tile node into game grid list
4. Set tile index field
5. Apply tile flags with 0x80000 visibility flag OR'd with provided flags
6. Fetch rendering data from game state via Ordinal_10010 (D2Gfx.DrawRect)
7. Copy rendering offsets from render data to unit structure (+0x64, +0x68)
8. Calculate distance-based rendering flags via FUN_6fd9bbb0() with render offsets
9. Store calculated flags at unit structure +0x6c
10. Return newly allocated tile node

Parameters:
pListHead (int) - Game grid tile list head/anchor node
nMinX (int) - Minimum X coordinate of tile bounding box
nMinY (int) - Minimum Y coordinate of tile bounding box
nMaxX (int) - Maximum X coordinate of tile bounding box
nMaxY (int) - Maximum Y coordinate of tile bounding box
dwFlags (uint) - Tile attribute flags to OR with 0x80000 visibility flag
dwExtraData1 (uint) - Extra rendering property #1 (written to +0x54)
dwExtraData2 (uint) - Extra rendering property #2 (written to +0x58)
nIndex (int) - Tile index identifier

Returns:
ListNode * - Newly allocated and initialized tile node, or NULL on failure

Special Cases:
Magic number 0x80000 - Visibility/active flag always set for all tiles
Rendering data fetched from current game state context (param_1 + 0x4 offset)
Distance calculation at offset +0x6c used for tile culling/LOD decisions

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x0 | 4 | nMinX | int | Tile bounding box minimum X
0x4 | 4 | nMinY | int | Tile bounding box minimum Y
0x8 | 4 | nMaxX | int | Tile bounding box maximum X
0xc | 4 | nMaxY | int | Tile bounding box maximum Y
0x10 | 4 | dwFlags | uint | Attribute flags with 0x80000 OR'd in
0x14 | 4 | pUnitData | int * | Pointer to detailed unit data
0x1c | 4 | pUnitData | int * | Secondary unit data pointer
0x20 | 4 | nIndex | int | Tile index identifier
0x54 | 4 | dwExtra1 | uint | Extra rendering property
0x58 | 4 | dwExtra2 | uint | Extra rendering property
0x64 | 4 | dwRender1 | uint | Render offset from state
0x68 | 4 | dwRender2 | uint | Render offset from state
0x6c | 4 | dwDistFlags | uint | Distance-based rendering flags

functions.name: ClearUnitInventorySlots
functions.comment:
Clear inventory and resource slots for a unit.

Algorithm:
1. Extract structure pointer from unit data offset 0x20 (ESI = [EBX + 0x20])
2. Get inventory type field from unit offset 0 ([EBX] -> [EAX] -> EDI at +0x4)
3. If structure exists (TEST ESI, ESI):
   a. Clear primary inventory fields at offsets +0x0, +0x14, +0x28, +0x3c via ClearStructureFields
   b. Clear linked list at offset +0x50 via ValidateAndClearLinkedListWithDebugOutput
   c. Log debug message via Ordinal_10046 (Storm.dbgmsg equivalent)
   d. Zero structure pointer in unit at offset 0x20

Parameters:
  pUnitData (dword *) - Pointer to unit structure
    Offset 0: Pointer to inventory type descriptor
    Offset 0x20: Pointer to inventory structure (cleared after cleanup)

Returns:
  void - Modifies unit structure in-place

Special Cases:
  NULL check: If structure pointer is NULL, skips all cleanup (JZ at 0x6fd94631)
  Magic constant: 0xad passed to debug log

Structure Layout (Inventory):
  Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
  0x00   | 4    | type       | dword| Inventory type identifier
  0x14   | 4    | field_20   | dword| Secondary inventory field
  0x28   | 4    | field_40   | dword| Tertiary inventory field
  0x3c   | 4    | field_60   | dword| Quaternary inventory field
  0x50   | ?    | linkedList | list | Linked list of inventory items

Related Functions:
- ClearStructureFields - Clears individual inventory field groups
- ValidateAndClearLinkedListWithDebugOutput - Clears linked list
- ClearUnitState - Calls this function to cleanup unit
- Ordinal_10046 - Storm.dll debug logging

functions.name: ClearLinkedListStructure
functions.comment:
Clears and validates linked list structure fields in a container.

Algorithm:
1. Load structure pointer from container[0x20]
2. Exit early if structure pointer is NULL
3. Load resource type ID from container[0x0] + 0x4
4. Call ClearStructureFields on field at offset +0x00
5. Call ClearStructureFields on field at offset +0x14
6. Call ClearStructureFields on field at offset +0x28
7. Call ClearStructureFields on field at offset +0x3c
8. Call ValidateAndClearLinkedListWithDebugOutput on linked list at +0x50

Parameters:
pListHeader: Pointer to container with embedded linked lists (passed in ECX via __fastcall)

Returns:
void: No return value; modifies structure in place

functions.name: AllocateAndZeroStructure
functions.comment:
Allocate and zero-initialize a structure buffer

Algorithm:
1. Call Ordinal_10045 to allocate 0xc5 bytes (197 bytes)
2. Zero the first 0x1c dwords (28 * 4 = 112 bytes)
3. Store allocated pointer at pStructPtr + 0x20 offset

Parameters:
pStructPtr - Pointer to structure containing offset field at +0x20

Returns:
void (pointer stored at pStructPtr + 0x20)

functions.name: InitializeUnitComponents
functions.comment:
Initialize all component structures for a unit entity.

Algorithm:
1. Call pre-initialization setup on unit
2. Retrieve data base pointer from unit[0x20]
3. Calculate offset pointers: offset +5 and +10 from data base
4. Initialize first component at offset +5 with FUN_6fd9a480
5. Initialize second component at offset +5 with FUN_6fd9a3b0
6. Initialize third component at offset +10 with FUN_6fd9a3b0
7. Call component setup function FUN_6fd9a5d0
8. Configure first component with FUN_6fd99560
9. Configure third component with FUN_6fd99560
10. Retrieve configuration struct from unit[0xa8]
11. Copy 3 configuration values: 0x8→0x18, 0xc→0x20, 0x10→0x28
12. Call game object initialization

Parameters:
pUnit (int *): Unit entity structure containing component configuration data

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Configuration structure offset values (0x8, 0xc, 0x10) are copied to output offsets (0x18, 0x20, 0x28)
- Multiple component initialization functions called sequentially for different data regions

Related Functions:
- InitializeGameObject() - Performs final game object setup after component initialization
- FUN_6fd9a590() - Pre-initialization setup called first
- FUN_6fd9a480(), FUN_6fd9a3b0() - Component structure initialization
- FUN_6fd9a5d0() - Component post-setup configuration
- FUN_6fd99560() - Component runtime configuration

functions.name: GetRoomPropertyFlags
functions.comment:
Extract room property flag (0x80) from room structure.

Algorithm:
1. Load room descriptor pointer from pRoom[0x20]
2. Load property flags from descriptor[0x54]
3. Mask with 0x80 to extract specific flag bit
4. Return flag value (0 if clear, 0x80 if set)

Parameters:
  pRoom (dword *): Pointer to room data structure

Returns:
  uint: Property flags with 0x80 bit value (0x00 or 0x80)

Magic Numbers:
  0x20: Offset to room descriptor pointer in room structure
  0x54: Offset to property flags in room descriptor
  0x80: Property flag mask bit

functions.name: SetUnitAnimationFrameOffsets
functions.comment:
Set unit animation frame offsets based on a property value.

Algorithm:
1. Call Ordinal_10917(pUnit) to get a property value
2. Extract lowest bit via (value & 1) - stores 0 or 1 in dwFrameIndex
3. Store dwFrameIndex at two unit property offsets (0x3f and 0x4e within indexed location)
4. Calculate frame data pointer: pUnit + (unit_index * 4) + 2
5. Branch on dwFrameIndex value:
   - If 0: Set frame offsets to (0x40, 0xa0)
   - If 1: Set frame offsets to (0xa0, 0x40)
6. Calculate source frame data from indexed location in unit structure
7. Compute frame coordinate X offset: pSourceFrameData[0] - pFrameData[2]
8. Compute frame coordinate Y offset: (pSourceFrameData[3] - pFrameData[3]) - 0x10 + pSourceFrameData[1]
9. Store computed offsets at pFrameData + 0/1
10. Return success (1)

Parameters:
- pUnit: Pointer to unit structure containing animation frame data

Returns:
- 1: Always succeeds

Magic Numbers:
- 0x7b: Unit property index offset (multiplied by 4 for dword access)
- 0x3e, 0x3f, 0x4e: Unit property storage offsets
- 0x40, 0xa0: Frame offset values (conditional based on parity)
- 0x10: Constant offset adjustment (-0x10 for Y calculation)

functions.name: ApplyOrientationTransform
functions.comment:
Apply orientation/rotation transform to entity display parameters.

Algorithm:
1. Query current orientation flag via Ordinal_10917 (returns 0 or 1)
2. Extract LSB as dwRotation (0=normal, 1=reversed)
3. Store dwRotation at two offset locations (0x7b + 0x3f and 0x7b + 0x4e)
4. Load base index from offset 0x7b
5. Update display parameters based on rotation state:
   - If dwRotation == 0: set offsets +4=0x40, +5=0xa0
   - If dwRotation == 1: set offsets +4=0xa0, +5=0x40
6. Query transform data via Ordinal_10010 with parameter at offset 0x7c
7. Copy transform fields from returned pointer:
   - Offset 0xc → data[index*4 + 2]
   - Offset 0x10 → data[index*4 + 3]
8. Return success (1)

Parameters:
pData: Pointer to main data structure containing rotation state, indices, and display parameters

Returns:
1 on success

Special Cases:
Magic values 0x40 and 0xa0 represent display coordinate thresholds for orientation.
Index accessed at offset 0x7b drives all array subscript calculations.

Magic Numbers:
0x1ec (508) - Offset to active index in data structure
0x1f0 (512) - Offset to transform lookup parameter
0x7b, 0x7c - Offsets within indexed structure
0x3f, 0x4e - Flag storage offsets (relative to index)
0x40 - Display parameter for normal orientation
0xa0 - Display parameter for reversed orientation
0xc, 0x10 - Field offsets in transform result

functions.name: UpdateViewportCoordinates
functions.comment:
Updates viewport coordinates based on state flags and linked viewport values.

Algorithm:
1. Read current viewport slot index from pViewport[0x7b]
2. Check if viewport state (at slot+0x4e) is uninitialized (0xffffffff)
3. If uninitialized: call Ordinal_10917() (D2Common.RandSeed), store low bit as state
4. If already initialized: check if display state differs from stored state
5. If states match, return 0 (no update needed)
6. Store new display state at slot+0x3f
7. Lookup linked viewport index from table at pViewport[0x3e]+8+(slot*0x10)
8. Get linked viewport's display state
9. Based on current state (0 or 1), set coordinate palette flags:
   - State 0: flags[slot*4+4]=0x40, flags[slot*4+5]=0xa0
   - State 1: flags[slot*4+4]=0xa0, flags[slot*4+5]=0x40
10. Combine states: tableIndex = currentState + linkedState*2
11. Load X offset from g_adCoordinateXTable[tableIndex*8]
12. Load Y offset from g_adCoordinateYTable[tableIndex*8]
13. Add offsets to linked viewport's coordinates and store in current viewport

Parameters:
pViewport (uint *) - Viewport structure containing:
  [0x3e] - Pointer to viewport array
  [0x7b] - Current viewport slot index
  [0xfc + slot*4] - Viewport slot state
  [0x138 + slot*4] - Viewport initialization flag
  [slot*4+2] - Viewport X coordinate
  [slot*4+3] - Viewport Y coordinate
  [slot*4+4,5] - Coordinate palette flags

Returns:
1 - Coordinates were updated
0 - Coordinates unchanged (state already matched)

Special Cases:
- First call: initializes state by calling Ordinal_10917()
- Coordinate lookup uses 2D indexing: base + (state + linkedState*2)*8
- Supports two coordinate palettes (states 0 and 1) with opposite flag settings
- Returns 0 immediately if viewport already in target state

Global Data:
- g_adCoordinateXTable - X coordinate offset lookup table (indexed by combined state)
- g_adCoordinateYTable - Y coordinate offset lookup table (indexed by combined state)

functions.name: ValidateLinePatternMarker
functions.comment:
Validates if marker equals diagonal line pattern sentinel (0x75).

Algorithm:
1. Load marker value from structure field at offset +4 bytes from base pointer
2. Compare loaded value against sentinel 0x75 (diagonal pattern identifier)
3. Set AL to 1 if values match (SETZ instruction), 0 if different
4. Add 0x04 base offset to comparison result
5. Return encoded result (0x05 if valid marker, 0x04 if invalid)

Parameters:
nMarker - int (fastcall ECX): Base address of structure; marker value read from +4 offset

Returns:
char: 0x05 if marker at [nMarker+4] == 0x75 (valid diagonal pattern)
      0x04 if marker at [nMarker+4] != 0x75 (invalid or different pattern)

Special Cases:
Magic value 0x75: Sentinel identifier for diagonal line pattern type
Return encoding: Uses 0x04 base with +1 offset for valid condition
Caller must validate pointer validity before call

functions.name: RenderInventoryGridWithTiles
functions.comment:
Renders inventory grid with dynamic tiles and slot ranges.

Algorithm:
1. If param_1[1] != 0x6e, process inventory slots using ProcessInventorySlotRange
2. Iterate through linked list of data node pointers from param_1[0xe]
3. For each node, extract coordinate offsets and lookup table values
4. Render tiles with RenderObjectAtCoordinates based on node flags
5. Check node flag 0x02 to determine render loop conditions
6. Apply offset adjustments based on flag 0x01 for additional tiles
7. Call specialized rendering functions (FUN_6fd94f80, FUN_6fd94e50, etc.)
8. If param_1[1] == 0x6e, render siege level tiles in 15-tile sequence

Parameters:
pGridData (uint *): Pointer to grid/inventory structure containing:
  [0xe] = Level data pointer
  [1] = Type/mode indicator (0x6e=siege, 0x75=special, 0x6f=extra)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Siege mode (param_1[1] == 0x6e) renders fixed 15-tile grid pattern
- Non-siege modes iterate through dynamic node list
- Flag 0x02 in node[3] controls render loop iteration
- Flag 0x01 in node[3] triggers additional tile offset rendering
- Note: Function uses 7 stack-allocated temporaries optimized away (SSA variables)

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x6e - Siege level type
0x75 - Special mode indicator
0x6f - Extra rendering trigger mode
0xfffffffe - Bitmask to clear low bit
0x4c, 0x371, 0x37d, 0x38a, 0x389 - Tile/sprite resource offsets
0x361 - Siege tile base resource ID (retrieved via Ordinal_10024)
0x60 - Level dimension offset
0x5c - Level base offset
0x24 - Preset definition size field
0x100, 0x400 - Dispatch flags for special rendering

Related Functions:
- ProcessInventorySlotRange() - Validates inventory slot data
- RenderObjectAtCoordinates() - Core tile rendering function
- CompareValuePairs() - Extract coordinate values
- GetLookupTableValue() - Retrieve tile sprite ID

functions.name: RenderInventoryGridTiles
functions.comment:
Render inventory grid tile objects with position offsets.

Algorithm:
1. Load base coordinate pointer from grid structure at offset 0x38
2. Initialize tile entry pointer to global tile array at 0x6fde1900
3. Loop through all tile entries (5-uint stride, up to 0x6fde193c):
   a. Check if tile's grid ID (entry[-4]) matches current grid ID (grid[+4])
   b. If match: Determine vertical offset based on height constraint
      - If grid height (grid[+0x2c]) < max height (grid[+0x28]): use upper position
      - Else: use lower position
   c. Calculate X/Y offsets based on tile dimension flags (entry[-2])
      - If flag 0: offset (0,2) or (2,0)
      - If flag != 0: offset calculated from base coords minus 2
   d. Load tile dimension from entry[-3] and tile ID from entry[0] or entry[-1]
   e. Call Ordinal_10024 with tile ID (unknown Diablo II function)
   f. Render tile with RenderObjectAtCoordinates
4. Advance to next tile entry (add 0x14 bytes)

Parameters:
pGrid (void *) - Pointer to inventory grid structure with fields at +0x4, +0x28, +0x2c, +0x38

Returns:
None (void)

Structure Layout (Inventory Grid):
Offset | Size | Field | Type | Description
0x4    | 4    | gridId | uint | Grid identifier for tile matching
0x28   | 4    | maxHeight | int | Maximum allowed grid height
0x2c   | 4    | curHeight | int | Current grid height
0x38   | 4    | pCoordBase | void * | Pointer to base coordinates structure

Global Tile Array (g_pInventoryTileArray @ 0x6fde1900):
Entry Structure (5 uint fields per entry, 0x14 bytes):
Offset | Field | Purpose
-0x10  | gridId | Tile grid ID filter
0      | tileId1 | Upper position tile ID
-0x4   | tileId2 | Lower position tile ID  
-0x8   | dimFlags | Dimension offset flag (0=standard, else=custom)
-0xc   | tileSize | Tile dimension/size

Magic Numbers:
0x38 - Base coordinates offset in grid structure
0x2c - Current height offset
0x28 - Max height offset
0x4 - Grid ID offset
0x14 - Tile entry stride (5 dwords)
0x5c - Coordinate offset for width calculations
0x60 - Coordinate offset for height calculations
2 - Standard tile offset value
0x6fde1900 - Global tile array base address
0x6fde193c - End of tile array (0x3c bytes after start)

functions.name: RenderInventoryBorders
functions.comment:
Render inventory border objects on all four edges.

Algorithm:
  1. Load grid dimensions pointer from pInventoryGrid[0x38]
  2. Scan top edge (row 0, columns 0 to width): iterate until finding first item with FLAG_BORDER (0x400) flag
  3. When top border found, call RenderObjectAtCoordinates with row, 0, layer 0x38d
  4. Scan bottom-right edge (row height-2, columns 0 to width): find first item with FLAG_BORDER
  5. When bottom-right border found, call RenderObjectAtCoordinates with col, height-2, layer 0x38c
  6. Scan left edge (column 0, rows 0 to height): find first item with FLAG_BORDER
  7. When left border found, call RenderObjectAtCoordinates with 0, row, layer 0x38e
  8. Scan bottom-left corner (row width-2, columns 0 to height): find first item with FLAG_BORDER
  9. When bottom-left border found, call RenderObjectAtCoordinates with width-2, col, layer 0x38b

Parameters:
  pInventoryGrid (IMPLICIT ECX): void * - Grid structure pointer containing dimensions and element array

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Layer value depends on pInventoryGrid[0x4] comparison: (pInventoryGrid[0x4] != 0x6e) ? 0 : -1
  - Each edge scan breaks immediately upon finding first border item
  - Grid width stored at pInventoryGrid[0x38][0x5c]
  - Grid height stored at pInventoryGrid[0x38][0x60]
  - Element array base at pInventoryGrid[0x38][0x2c]

Note: Function uses 2 stack-allocated temporaries (dVar1, iVar2) optimized away by compiler

functions.name: DispatchInventoryGridBorderRendering
functions.comment:
Dispatch rendering calls for inventory grid borders.

Algorithm:
1. Load border element index from grid structure field at offset 0x38, then 0x60
2. Call DispatchIndexedFunction with (index - 4) and flag 0x400
3. Call DispatchIndexedFunction with (index - 3) and flag 0x400
4. Return to caller

Parameters:
nGridPtr (int) - IMPLICIT[ECX] Pointer to inventory grid structure

Returns:
void - No return value, modifies render state via function dispatch calls

Special Cases:
- Border index is adjusted by subtracting 4 or 3 before dispatch
- Both calls use flag 0x400 (render grid borders)
- Called only when grid type is 0x6f (custom grid)

functions.name: RenderInventoryGridPostprocess
functions.comment:
Initialize and dispatch final inventory grid rendering pass. Postprocessing step that builds parameter array with function dispatch pointers and invokes grid rendering pipeline.

Algorithm:
1. Check if grid type is NOT 0x6e (exit early if so)
2. Retrieve base data pointer from pGridData[0xe]
3. Zero-initialize 14-dword array (adwRenderParams) for parameter passing
4. Calculate and store three offset pointers:
   - nDataOffset1 = base + 0x04
   - nDataOffset2 = base + 0x54
   - nDataOffset3 = base + 0x2c
5. Populate function pointer array with dispatch handlers:
   - pfnRenderLabel = address of rendering label data
   - pfnDispatchIndexed = DispatchDualIndexedFunction reference
   - pfnDispatchAction = DispatchGameObjectActions reference
   - pfnRenderObject = RenderObjectAtCoordinates reference
   - pfnLookupOffset = LookupCharacterEncodingOffset reference
6. Set magic values:
   - dwMagicInvalid = 0xffffffff (invalid marker)
   - dwRenderCount = 0x0c (12 render iterations)
7. Store pGridData reference in adwRenderParams[0]
8. Call FUN_6fd9a9e0 with parameter array
9. Return

Parameters:
pGridData - Pointer to inventory grid structure (pass via ECX per __fastcall)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
Grid type validation: Function returns immediately if pGridData[1] == 0x6e without performing rendering

functions.name: LookupCharacterEncodingOffset
functions.signature: int LookupCharacterEncodingOffset(int * ppEncodingTable, int nEncodingStyle, int nCharacterIndex)
functions.comment:
Search encoding table for matching style and character index bounds

Algorithm:
1. Validate encoding style is 0x30 or 0x31 (0x30='0', 0x31='1')
2. Iterate through encoding table entries (stride of 5 dwords per entry)
3. For each entry: check if style matches param_2 AND character index falls within bounds [piVar1[1], piVar1[2]]
4. If match found, calculate offset relative to table bounds based on flag at param_1[+4]
   - If flag == 0x75: return (piVar1[4] - piVar1[1]) + nCharacterIndex
   - Otherwise: return (piVar1[3] - piVar1[1]) + nCharacterIndex
5. If no match found or bounds check fails, assert and exit with -1

Parameters:
- ppEncodingTable (ECX): Pointer to encoding table (array of 5-dword entries)
- wEncodingStyle (EDX): Encoding style flag (0x30 or 0x31, ASCII characters)
- nCharacterIndex (Stack+0x4): Character index to look up

Returns:
- int: Calculated offset into encoding data, or assertion/exit if invalid

Magic Numbers:
- 0x30, 0x31: Valid encoding style values ('0' and '1' in ASCII)
- 0x75: Flag threshold for selecting offset calculation method
- 0x6fde1990: Start of global encoding table
- 0x6fde1a57: Upper bound of encoding table range

Special Cases:
- Invalid encoding style triggers D2Common_DbgAssertion() which calls FUN_6fdd5a09 (non-returning)
- Table iteration overflow also triggers assertion
- Function returns via RET with 4-byte parameter cleanup

functions.name: ProcessInventoryGridConfigurations
functions.comment:
Iterate through grid configuration table and render inventory grid tiles based on unit dimensions.

Algorithm:
1. Load unit min/max stats from parameter structure (offsets 0x28, 0x2c)
2. Initialize pointer to grid configuration table (g_pGridConfigTable)
3. For each grid configuration entry in table:
   a. Check if grid config ID matches unit ID (param + 0x4)
   b. If match found, select grid start coordinates based on unit stats comparison
   c. Load grid start Y coordinate and tile count from configuration
   d. Initialize tile index counter to 0
   e. While tile index < tile count: call ValidateAndRenderGridPoints() to render each tile
   f. Check return value; if non-zero, break to error handling
   g. Check configuration error flag (offset +0x14)
   h. If error flag set, call D2Common_DbgAssertion() and FUN_6fdd5a09(-1)
4. Advance to next configuration entry (+0x1c stride)
5. Stop iteration when pointer exceeds end boundary (0x6fde1c08)

Parameters:
  pGridUnit (ECX): Pointer to inventory grid unit structure
    - Offset 0x04: Grid configuration ID
    - Offset 0x28: Unit min stat value
    - Offset 0x2c: Unit max stat value

Returns:
  void (no return value, performs rendering as side effect)

Special Cases:
  - If unit min stat >= max stat, uses alternate grid coordinate set
  - Configuration table is linear array with 7-dword entries (0x1c bytes each)
  - Error flag at config offset +0x14 triggers assertion and process exit
  - Tile count at config offset +0x10 determines iteration count

functions.name: RenderPrisonGridObjects
functions.comment:
Renders prison objects on a grid with scrolling pattern detection.

Algorithm:
1. Validate unit type is 0x6f (Prison) and level data exists
2. Get player grid dimensions from level data (0x5c=width, 0x60=height)
3. Calculate initial grid position via RNG (Ordinal_10918)
4. First scan (0x5a iterations): Find up to 2 prison objects near player position
5. If less than 2 objects found, scan entire grid using modulo wrapping
6. For each grid cell: Check object type range [0x392..0x39a], render if matched
7. Stop when 3 objects rendered or grid exhausted (max render limit)
8. If less than 3 prisons placed, log warning via Ordinal_10025

Parameters:
pUnit: Pointer to player unit (type checked for 0x6f at offset 0x4)

Returns:
void - Side effects only (rendering)

Special Cases:
0x5a = 90 decimal - Initial scan iteration limit
0x392..0x39a = 914..922 decimal - Prison object type range
0x10 = Offset added to object type for rendering (0x392+0x10=0x3a2)
Max 3 objects rendered per call (safety limit)
Returns early if 3+ objects already rendered during grid scan

Note: Function uses 2 compiler-optimized temporaries (SSA variables) not directly accessible
string_refs: "Could not place enough prisons for quest 2. Pleas...

functions.name: RenderPresetDoodads
functions.comment:
Validates and renders preset doodads/objects in a level at computed screen coordinates

Algorithm:
1. Validate input level pointer is not NULL (assert and exit if NULL)
2. Validate level ID field at offset +0x4 equals 0x6f (LEVEL_ID magic, assert if mismatch)
3. Load level data pointer from offset +0x38 (assert and exit if NULL)
4. Call Ordinal_10024(0x370) to get preset definition table (assert and exit if NULL)
5. Load level base X coordinate from level data at offset +0x5c
6. Load level base Y coordinate from level data at offset +0x60
7. Load preset tile X offset from preset definition at offset +0x24, apply signed division: (x + sign_extend) >> 3
8. Load preset tile Y offset from preset definition at offset +0x28, apply signed division: (y + sign_extend) >> 3
9. Compute screen X = baseX - (presetX >> 3)
10. Compute screen Y = baseY - (presetY >> 3)
11. Render preset object type 0x370 at computed (screenX, screenY)
12. Render preset object type 0x380 at computed (screenX, screenY-2)

Parameters:
  nLevel (int): Level structure pointer containing tile coordinates and data references

Returns:
  void: Function exits via tail calls to RenderObjectAtCoordinates, no direct return value

Magic Numbers:
  0x6f - LEVEL_ID validation magic number
  0x370 - Preset object tile type 1 identifier
  0x380 - Preset object tile type 2 identifier
  0x24, 0x28 - Preset definition offsets for tile X and Y coordinates
  0x5c, 0x60 - Level data offsets for base screen X and Y coordinates
  0x38 - Level data pointer offset within level structure

functions.name: FindViewportTileElement
functions.signature: void FindViewportTileElement(int nViewport, int * pnOutElementOffset, int * pnOutSubIndex)
functions.comment:
Search viewport tile array for first element with specific rendering properties.

Algorithm:
1. Load viewport data base address from ECX+0x38
2. Calculate maximum element count = (field[0x5c]/2) - 1
3. Initialize search index to 1
4. Iterate while index < max count:
   a. Call GetNestedArrayElement(base+4, offset, index) -> dwElementValue
   b. Call GetNestedArrayElement(base+0x2c, offset, index) -> dwFieldValue
   c. Check if dwElementValue == 0x1c AND (dwFieldValue >> 0x10 & 0xf) == 1
   d. If match found, write offset and index to output parameters and return
   e. Increment index and continue
5. If no match found, write -1 to both output parameters

Parameters:
pViewport - viewport structure pointer (fast call: ECX)
pnOutElementOffset - pointer to output element offset result (fast call: EDX)
pnOutSubIndex - pointer to output sub-index result (stack param)

Returns:
Void. Results written to *pnOutElementOffset and *pnOutSubIndex:
- If match found: offset and index of element matching criteria
- If no match: -1 in both output locations

Special Cases:
- Empty or single-element viewports return -1
- Magic value 0x1c indicates specific rendering property
- High nibble (bits 16-19) of field[0x2c] must be 1 for match

functions.name: RenderAndProcessGameUI
functions.comment:
RenderAndProcessGameUI - Render UI elements and process inventory/quest grid rendering

Algorithm:
1. If UI type is 2, 3, or 0x11: skip main list processing and proceed to step 5
2. Load base config pointer from pUIState[0xe]
3. Iterate through linked list of UI elements starting at config[0x19]
4. For each element, check if rendering conditions met (coordinate comparisons, flag checks)
5. If conditions pass, find last valid element and mark elements with flag 0x01 up to that point
6. Set flag 0x20 on config when update complete
7. Process inventory slots via ProcessInventorySlotRange()
8. Render diagonal line pattern via RenderDiagonalLinePattern()
9. If UI type in range [2,7]: call UpdateQuestUIPanel() for quest display
10. If flag 0x20 set and flag 0x40 not set: process grid rendering (Ordinal_10917 button state)
11. Iterate through grid cells row-by-row, call FUN_6fd95b40() for each cell
12. If error, log via Ordinal_10025() with source line 0x193
13. If flags 0x1c set but 0x40 not set: render object at adjusted coordinates
14. Call UpdateQuestUIPanel() for all panels, ProcessQuestGridLayout(), ShuffleCoordinatePairs()
15. If UI type 0x27: update all quest panels
16. Call FUN_6fd95cd0() for final cleanup

Parameters:
  pUIState (int *) - Pointer to UI state structure containing:
    [1] = UI type/panel ID (determines rendering flow)
    [0xe] = Config pointer with flags and grid dimensions
    [0x18] = Grid height (rows)
    [0x17] = Grid width (columns)
    [0x19] = Linked list head for elements

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - UI types 2, 3, 0x11 skip element list processing
  - Coordinate checks validate element positioning before rendering
  - Grid iteration depends on Ordinal_10917() button state (affects column/row order)
  - Magic flag 0x20 indicates update needed, 0x40 indicates processing in progress

Magic Numbers:
  0x11 - Special UI type identifier
  0x27 - Special quest panel mode
  0x1c - Rendering flags mask
  0x20 - Update required flag
  0x40 - Processing in progress flag
  0x0c - Movement flag check
  0x64 - Offset to list head in config
  0x5c - Grid width field offset
  0x60 - Grid height field offset
  0x193 - Source code line number for logging

functions.name: ValidateArrayElementFlags
functions.comment:
Validates that array elements at specified indices don't have restricted flag set.

Algorithm:
1. Load array structure pointer from input parameter at offset 0x38
2. Get array element count from structure offset 0x60
3. Loop through all array elements using counter starting at 0
4. For each iteration, check both nIndex and nIndex+1 elements:
   a. Call GetNestedArrayElement for current index pair
   b. Check if flags bit 0x2 is set (AND with 2)
   c. Return 0 (FAILURE) if bit is set for either element
5. Increment loop counter and continue until all elements checked
6. Return 1 (SUCCESS) if all elements pass validation

Parameters:
