functions.name: InitializeDirectoryEntry
functions.signature: dword * InitializeDirectoryEntry(int nContextHandle, int nDirectoryId, dword * pSourceArray, dword dwSourceValue, dword nRoomAdjacencyId, dword dwRoomFlags)
functions.comment:
Allocate and initialize a directory entry structure for a game room

Algorithm:
1. Validate context handle (param_1) is non-zero; assert failure if null
2. Allocate directory entry memory (32 dwords) via Ordinal_10045 debug allocator
3. Zero-fill entire entry with REP STOSD (32 × 4 bytes)
4. Initialize fields: [0x12]=dwRoomFlags, [0xF]=nRoomAdjacencyId, [0xE]=nDirectoryId
5. Copy source array (8 dwords) starting at offset 0; source at pSourceArray
6. Set field [8]=dwSourceValue; field [0x1F]=prev pointer from context[+4]
7. Link new entry into context list: context[+4] → pDirectoryEntry
8. Set context[+0x20]=1 (mark initialized); link entry back to context[+0x1E]
9. Call SetDirectoryPath to configure file path via context[+0x5C]
10. Allocate output buffer (0xDE size) for room data via Ordinal_10045
11. Copy non-zero elements from source room data to output buffer via CopyNonzeroArrayElements
12. Process room adjacency list: for each adjacent room, copy its non-zero elements
13. Assert each adjacent entry is valid; skip if matches self reference
14. Initialize room from directory via InitializeRoomFromDirectory
15. If context callback (context[+0x18]) exists, invoke it

Parameters:
  nContextHandle (int): Game/context handle; fields at +4, +0x18, +0x20, +0x5C, +0xE
  nDirectoryId (int): Room directory ID stored at offset 0xE
  pSourceArray (dword *): Pointer to 8-dword source array to copy at offset 0
  dwSourceValue (dword): Value stored at offset 8
  nRoomAdjacencyId (dword): Room adjacency ID stored at offset 0xF via Ordinal_10913
  dwRoomFlags (dword): Room flags stored at offset 0x12

Returns:
  dword *: Pointer to initialized directory entry structure (occupancy: 32 dwords, ~128 bytes)

Special Cases:
  - Entry assertion at [0xF] if adjacent room pointer null; terminates with Ordinal_10913
  - Assertion if context handle is zero; terminates with FUN_6fdd5a09(0xFFFFFFFF)
  - Output buffer allocation size: 0xDE (222 bytes)
  - List linkage: context[+4] forms doubly-linked list via [0x1F]=prev, [0x1E]=context ptr

functions.name: RectanglesIntersect
functions.comment:
Validates that two axis-aligned rectangles have overlapping regions.

Algorithm:
1. Assert pRectA is not null; exit with fatal error if null
2. Assert pRectB is not null; exit with fatal error if null
3. Check horizontal bounds: if pRectB.x + pRectB.width < pRectA.x, no overlap
4. Check horizontal bounds: if pRectA.x + pRectA.width < pRectB.x, no overlap
5. Check vertical bounds: if pRectB.y + pRectB.height < pRectA.y, no overlap
6. Check vertical bounds: if pRectB.y <= pRectA.y + pRectA.height, rectangles intersect
7. Return true if all bounds pass, false otherwise

Parameters:
pRectA: Pointer to Rectangle A structure containing position and dimensions
pRectB: Pointer to Rectangle B structure containing position and dimensions

Returns:
true: Rectangles have overlapping area
false: Rectangles do not overlap

functions.name: IsPointInRoom
functions.signature: uint IsPointInRoom(RoomBounds * pRoom, int nX, int nY)
functions.comment:
Check if coordinates are within room bounds.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input room pointer is non-null (call assertion if NULL)
2. Load room x_min from offset 0x10 into ECX register
3. Load X coordinate (nX) from stack parameter into EDX
4. Compare if X >= x_min, branch to false return if X < x_min
5. Load x_width from offset 0x18, add to x_min to calculate x_max
6. Compare if X < x_max, branch to false return if X >= x_max
7. Load room y_min from offset 0x14 into ECX register
8. Load Y coordinate (nY) from stack parameter into EDX
9. Compare if Y >= y_min, branch to false return if Y < y_min
10. Load y_width from offset 0x1c, add to y_min to calculate y_max
11. Compare if Y < y_max, branch to false return if Y >= y_max
12. Return 1 (true) if both conditions satisfied, otherwise return 0 (false)

Parameters:
  pRoom: Pointer to RoomBounds structure with x/y min/width at offsets 0x10, 0x14, 0x18, 0x1c
  nX: Integer X coordinate to validate
  nY: Integer Y coordinate to validate

Returns:
  uint: 1 (true) if point (nX, nY) is within room area, 0 (false) if outside bounds

Special Cases:
  - Asserts if pRoom pointer is NULL instead of returning false
  - Both X and Y must satisfy bounds checks to return true
  - Calculates maximum as (min + width) and checks X < max, Y < max

Structure Layout (RoomBounds at pRoom):
  Offset  | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
  --------|------|------------|------|----------------------------------------------
  0x10    | 4    | xMin       | int  | Minimum X coordinate of room area
  0x14    | 4    | yMin       | int  | Minimum Y coordinate of room area
  0x18    | 4    | xWidth     | int  | Width of room in X direction
  0x1c    | 4    | yWidth     | int  | Height of room in Y direction

functions.name: Ordinal_10048
functions.comment:
Validates buffer consistency by checking two offset pair sums for overflow detection.

Algorithm:
1. Assert input buffer pointer is non-null; crash if NULL via D2Common_DbgAssertion
2. Load first offset pair: dwStartOffset1 @ [pOffsetBuffer+0x10], dwEndOffset1 @ [pOffsetBuffer+0x18]
3. Calculate first sum: dwEndOffset1 += dwStartOffset1
4. Check for overflow: if (dwEndOffset1 < dwStartOffset1) return 0 (inconsistent state detected)
5. Load second offset pair: dwStartOffset2 @ [pOffsetBuffer+0x14], dwEndOffset2 @ [pOffsetBuffer+0x1c]
6. Calculate second sum: dwEndOffset2 += dwStartOffset2
7. Check for overflow: if (dwEndOffset2 < dwStartOffset2) return 0 (inconsistent state detected)
8. Compare first pair: if (dwStartOffset1 == dwEndOffset1) return 1 (perfect balance in first pair)
9. Compare second pair and return: if (dwStartOffset2 == dwEndOffset2) return 3 else return 4

Parameters:
- pOffsetBuffer (OffsetPairBuffer *): Pointer to buffer containing two offset pair fields for validation

Returns:
- 0x00: Overflow detected in either offset pair (integer overflow indicates corruption)
- 0x01: First pair sum matches (dwStartOffset1 == dwEndOffset1 sum)
- 0x03: Second pair sum matches (dwStartOffset2 == dwEndOffset2 sum)
- 0x04: Second pair sums differ (normal case when pairs unequal)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x10: Offset to dwStartOffset1 field
- 0x14: Offset to dwStartOffset2 field
- 0x18: Offset to dwEndOffset1 field
- 0x1c: Offset to dwEndOffset2 field

functions.name: Ordinal_10051
functions.signature: void * Ordinal_10051(void * pHead, int nX, int nY)
functions.comment:
Search linked list for rect node containing point.

Algorithm:
1. Load head pointer from pHead->next at offset 0x4
2. Loop through linked list until pCurrent == NULL, return 0
3. For each node, check if point (nX, nY) is within rect bounds
4. Verify X bounds: node[0x10] <= nX < node[0x10] + node[0x18]
5. Verify Y bounds: node[0x14] <= nY < node[0x14] + node[0x1c]
6. If all conditions pass, return pCurrent node pointer
7. Otherwise, advance to next node at offset 0x7c and repeat

Parameters:
- pHead (void *): Head of rect node list, actual list starts at offset 0x4
- nX (int): X coordinate of point to search for
- nY (int): Y coordinate of point to search for

Returns:
- Pointer to rect node if point found within bounds
- NULL (0) if no containing rect found or list is empty

Special Cases:
- Point on rect edge (nX == max_x) is outside bounds
- Point on rect edge (nY == max_y) is outside bounds
- Empty list or NULL head pointer returns 0
- List traversal uses offset 0x7c for next pointer

Structure Layout:
  Offset | Size | Field  | Type   | Description
  0x4    | 4    | pNext  | void * | Pointer to first rect node
  0x10   | 4    | x_min  | int    | Left boundary
  0x14   | 4    | y_min  | int    | Top boundary
  0x18   | 4    | width  | int    | Width
  0x1c   | 4    | height | int    | Height
  0x7c   | 4    | pNext  | void * | Next node pointer

functions.name: GetTile
functions.signature: int GetTile(int * ptRoomData, int nGameX, int nGameY)
functions.comment:
Find room structure containing game coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Validate ptRoomData pointer is non-null; exit if null with assertion
2. Load room count from ptRoomData[0x28] into loop bounds
3. If count is 0, skip iteration and return NULL
4. Get room array pointer from ptRoomData[0x24]
5. Initialize loop counter to 0
6. For each room in array until counter reaches count:
   a. Load room pointer from array[counter]
   b. Validate room pointer is non-null; exit if null with assertion
   c. Load room X bounds: xMin=[room+0x10], xSize=[room+0x18], xMax=xMin+xSize
   d. Check if nGameX >= xMin AND nGameX < xMax; if false, test next room
   e. Load room Y bounds: yMin=[room+0x14], ySize=[room+0x1c], yMax=yMin+ySize
   f. Check if nGameY >= yMin AND nGameY < yMax; if both true, return room pointer
   g. Increment counter and move to next array element
7. If no room found after full iteration, return NULL

Parameters:
ptRoomData (int *) - Pointer to room collection; array of room pointers at +0x24, count at +0x28
nGameX (int) - Game X coordinate to search for
nGameY (int) - Game Y coordinate to search for

Returns:
int * - Pointer to room structure if coordinates found within any room, else NULL
Calls D2Common_DbgAssertion and terminates process on NULL pointer dereference

functions.name: Ordinal_10049
functions.signature: void Ordinal_10049(Room * pRoom, int * pfnCallback, uint dwUserData)
functions.comment:
Iterate over room elements and invoke callback function on each.

Algorithm:
 1. Validate pRoom parameter is non-NULL, assert if NULL
 2. Validate pfnCallback is valid executable address using IsBadCodePtr
 3. Initialize loop counter dwIndex to 0
 4. Load element count from room structure at offset 0x28
 5. If element count is 0, return immediately (no elements to process)
 6. Load element array pointer from room structure at offset 0x24
 7. Get element at [array + dwIndex*4]
 8. Invoke callback(element, dwUserData) with return value in EAX
 9. If callback returns 0, exit function (element processing failed)
 10. Increment dwIndex and repeat loop until dwIndex >= count

Parameters:
 pRoom: Pointer to room structure containing element array
  - Offset 0x24: Pointer to element array (uint array)
  - Offset 0x28: Element count (uint)
 pfnCallback: Function pointer to callback, returns non-zero on success or zero to stop
 dwUserData: User-defined data passed to each callback invocation

Returns:
 void; Assertion failure if pRoom NULL or pfnCallback invalid (calls FUN_6fdd5a09)
 Early return if callback returns 0; Normal return if callback succeeds for all

functions.name: GetRoomRectangle
functions.comment:
Calculate axis-aligned bounding box of a room in isometric coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pRoom pointer is not NULL; fail if invalid
2. Load room base coordinates from pRoom->x (offset 0x10) and pRoom->y (offset 0x14)
3. Calculate bottom-left corner: Call Ordinal_10115(room.x, room.y, temp, pnBounds[0])
4. Calculate top-left corner: Call Ordinal_10115(room.x, room.y+room.height, pnBounds, temp)
5. Calculate bottom-right corner: Call Ordinal_10115(room.x+room.width, room.y, pnBounds[2], temp)
6. Calculate top-right corner: Call Ordinal_10115(room.x+room.width, room.y+room.height, temp, pnBounds[3])
7. Validate bounds: pnBounds[3] >= pnBounds[1] (top must be >= top-right)
8. Validate bounds: pnBounds[2] >= pnBounds[0] (right must be >= left)
9. Return success on validation pass; assertion failure and termination on validation fail

Parameters:
pRoom (int *): Pointer to isometric room structure
  - Offset 0x10: room base X coordinate
  - Offset 0x14: room base Y coordinate
  - Offset 0x18: room width (in isometric units)
  - Offset 0x1C: room height (in isometric units)
pnBounds (int *): Output array for 4 bounding box corner coordinates
  - pnBounds[0]: Bottom-left X
  - pnBounds[1]: Top-left Y
  - pnBounds[2]: Bottom-right X
  - pnBounds[3]: Top-right Y

Returns:
void; never returns on validation failure (calls FUN_6fdd5a09 which terminates)

Calls:
- Ordinal_10115: Converts isometric room coordinates to Cartesian screen coordinates (called 4x for each corner)
- D2Common_DbgAssertion: Validates preconditions and postconditions
- FUN_6fdd5a09: Fatal error handler (terminates if validation fails)

Special Cases:
- If pRoom is NULL, calls D2Common_DbgAssertion at line 0x1ae and exits
- If bounding box bounds are violated, calls assertions (lines 0x1b8, 0x1b9) and exits
- Assertion failures do not return to caller

functions.name: Ordinal_10053
functions.comment:
Copy and validate rectangle/region coordinates from source to destination.

Algorithm:
1. Validate source rectangle pointer is not NULL
2. Copy source rectangle's Y-offset (field[1]) to destination
3. Calculate destination bottom (Y-offset + height, field[3])
4. Copy source rectangle's left X (field[0]) to destination
5. Load source width (field[2]) and left X (field[0])
6. Calculate destination right (left + width, field[2])
7. Compare destination bottom against destination Y-offset - verify bottom >= top
8. Compare destination right against destination left - verify right >= left
9. Return if validation passes

Parameters:
pSrcRect (int *) - Pointer to source rectangle structure [left, top, width, height]
pDstRect (int *) - Pointer to destination rectangle structure to populate

Returns:
void - No return value; asserts and terminates if validation fails

Special Cases:
- NULL source pointer triggers assertion and fatal exit via FUN_6fdd5a09(-1)
- Invalid rectangle geometry (inverted bounds) triggers assertions at lines 0x1c9, 0x1ca

Structure Layout (Rectangle):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x0    | 4    | left       | int  | Left X coordinate
0x4    | 4    | top        | int  | Top Y coordinate
0x8    | 4    | width      | int  | Width in pixels
0xC    | 4    | height     | int  | Height in pixels

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1c1 - Assertion line number for NULL source check
0x1c9 - Assertion line number for inverted vertical bounds
0x1ca - Assertion line number for inverted horizontal bounds

functions.name: Ordinal_10054
functions.signature: void Ordinal_10054(UnitAny * pUnit, byte * pbR, byte * pbG, byte * pbB, byte * pbA)
functions.comment:
Extract RGBA color components from a unit entity.

Algorithm:
1. Load function pointer from unit structure at offset 0x38 (virtual method)
2. Prepare parameters: unit pointer and three color output buffers
3. Call virtual color extraction function
4. Return with RGBA values populated in output parameters

Parameters:
pUnit - UnitAny* - Pointer to unit entity structure
pbR - byte* - Output buffer for red component value (0-255)
pbG - byte* - Output buffer for green component value (0-255)
pbB - byte* - Output buffer for blue component value (0-255)
pbA - byte* - Output buffer for alpha component value (0-255)

Returns:
void - Color component values written to output buffers, no return code

Related Functions:
- GetColorComponentsFromEntity() - Virtual method implementation called indirectly

functions.name: FindRegionByCoordinates
functions.signature: int * FindRegionByCoordinates(int * pRegionRoot, int nX, int nY)
functions.comment:
Find region in hierarchy containing point coordinates.

Algorithm:
1. Validate root region pointer non-null
2. Check if target coordinates within root region bounds
3. If match found in root, return root pointer immediately
4. Iterate through child regions array (stored at offset 0x24/0x28)
5. For each child: validate pointer, check coordinate bounds
6. Return first matching child region or NULL if no match

Parameters:
pRegionRoot - pointer to root region structure (IMPLICIT register: EAX from ESP+0x4)
nX - X coordinate to search (IMPLICIT register: EBX from ESP+0x1c)
nY - Y coordinate to search (IMPLICIT register: EBP from ESP+0x18)

Returns:
int * - pointer to matching region structure, or NULL (0) if coordinates not found in any region

Structure Layout - Region:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x00   | 4    | x_min      | int  | Left boundary
0x04   | 4    | y_min      | int  | Top boundary
0x08   | 4    | x_span     | int  | Width (relative to x_min)
0x0c   | 4    | y_span     | int  | Height (relative to y_min)
0x24   | 4    | children   | int* | Pointer to child region array
0x28   | 4    | numChild   | int  | Count of child regions

functions.name: FindRectAtPoint
functions.signature: Rectangle * FindRectAtPoint(RectangleList * pRectList, int nX, int nY)
functions.comment:
Find rectangle containing point

Algorithm:
1. Check if pRectList is valid
2. Load rectangle pointer from pRectList->pFirstRect
3. Iterate through linked list of rectangles
4. For each rectangle, verify point is within bounds:
   a. Check nX >= rect->x AND nX < rect->x + rect->width
   b. Check nY >= rect->y AND nY < rect->y + rect->height
5. Return matching rectangle pointer if found
6. Load next rectangle from rect->pNext (offset 0x7c)
7. Continue until end of list (NULL)
8. Return NULL if no match

Parameters:
pRectList - RectangleList* - Rectangle list header
nX - int - X coordinate
nY - int - Y coordinate

Returns:
Rectangle* - Matching rectangle or NULL

functions.name: IsPointInRectangle
functions.signature: int IsPointInRectangle(int * pRect, int nX, int nY)
functions.comment:
Checks if a point (x, y) falls within a rectangular region.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pRect pointer is non-NULL (assertion failure if NULL)
2. Check if nX is within horizontal bounds: pRect[0] <= nX < pRect[0] + pRect[2]
3. Check if nY is within vertical bounds: pRect[1] <= nY < pRect[1] + pRect[3]
4. Return 1 if both conditions true, 0 otherwise

Parameters:
  pRect - Pointer to rectangle structure with 4 int fields:
    [0] = min_x (left edge)
    [1] = min_y (top edge)
    [2] = width (extent from min_x)
    [3] = height (extent from min_y)
  nX - X coordinate to test
  nY - Y coordinate to test

Returns:
  1 if (nX, nY) is within rectangle bounds (inclusive min, exclusive max)
  0 if point is outside bounds

Special Cases:
  - Asserts if pRect is NULL (calls D2Common_DbgAssertion)
  - Uses inclusive-exclusive bounds: [min, min+size)
  - Bounds checking prevents integer overflow on coordinate comparison

Structure Layout:
  Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
  0x0    | 4    | min_x      | int  | Left edge coordinate
  0x4    | 4    | min_y      | int  | Top edge coordinate
  0x8    | 4    | width      | int  | Horizontal extent
  0xC    | 4    | height     | int  | Vertical extent

functions.name: ValidateAndProcessUnitAuraState
functions.signature: void ValidateAndProcessUnitAuraState(UnitAny * pUnit, int nSlot, int nAuraState, int * pnResult1, int * pnResult2)
functions.comment:
Validates unit pointer and updates aura state for a unit slot.

Algorithm:
1. Load pUnit from stack parameter [ESP+0x4]
2. Test pUnit against zero (NULL check)
3. If pUnit is NULL: push assertion line 0x218, source file path, assertion text; call D2Common_DbgAssertion
4. After assertion call: push error code 0xffffffff; call FUN_6fdd5a09 (fatal exit handler)
5. If pUnit is not NULL: load aura array pointer from pUnit->data[0x8]
6. Push output parameters pnResult2, nAuraState, nSlot, and array pointer onto stack
7. Call ProcessUnitSlotAuraState to update aura state
8. Return to caller with __stdcall cleanup (pop 0x14 bytes)

Parameters:
- pUnit (UnitAny *): Pointer to unit structure containing aura data. Must not be NULL.
- nSlot (int): Slot index for aura update
- nAuraState (int): New aura state value to apply
- pnResult1 (int *): Output pointer for result value 1
- pnResult2 (int *): Output pointer for result value 2

Returns:
- void: No return value; results stored in output pointers pnResult1, pnResult2

functions.name: Ordinal_10045
functions.signature: int * Ordinal_10045(int nUnit, int nAuraType, int nAuraState, int * pnOutX, int * pnOutY, int nRandomSeed)
functions.comment:
Find spawn location for unit aura effect. Processes aura state to locate valid coordinates within a region, handling edge cases with coordinate adjustment.

Algorithm:
1. Validate unit pointer (nUnit) - assert if NULL, exit with status -1
2. Extract unit data pointer from nUnit + 8 offset
3. Call ProcessUnitSlotAuraState with aura type/state to get base coordinates
4. If aura processing failed (returns NULL), return NULL (no valid location found)
5. Call Ordinal_10113 (coordinate validation) on base coordinates
6. Adjust coordinates by +3 pixels in both X and Y directions (nResultX, nResultY)
7. Call Ordinal_10134 (spawn location finder) with adjusted coordinates and flag 0x1c09
8. If spawn location search failed (returns 0), assert and exit with status -1
9. Write adjusted X coordinate to output (pnOutX)
10. Write adjusted Y coordinate to output (pnOutY)
11. Find region containing final coordinates via FindRegionByCoordinates
12. Return region pointer; if aura processing failed, return NULL

Parameters:
- nUnit (int): Unit pointer for aura effect processing
- nAuraType (int): Aura/effect type identifier
- nAuraState (int): State flag for aura effect processing
- pnOutX (int *): Output - adjusted X coordinate after +3 pixel adjustment
- pnOutY (int *): Output - adjusted Y coordinate after +3 pixel adjustment
- nRandomSeed (int): Random seed value passed to spawn location finder

Returns:
- Region pointer if spawn location found and region exists
- NULL if aura processing failed or no valid location available

Special Cases:
- Coordinate adjustment (+3): Applied after spawn location calculation, likely accounts for unit size/collision
- Flag 0x1c09: Special flag passed to Ordinal_10134 controlling spawn location search behavior
- Unit assertion: NULL unit pointer triggers debug assertion and immediate exit

Magic Numbers:
- 0x8: Unit structure field offset to data pointer
- 0x3: Coordinate adjustment value (applied to both X and Y)
- 0x1c09: Spawn location finder flag (controls search criteria)
- -1 (0xFFFFFFFF): Fatal error exit code

Note: Function uses 3 stack-allocated temporaries optimized away in decompiled code (assembly-only variables).
string_refs: "Unable to find spawn location for act start"

functions.name: Ordinal_10029
functions.comment:
Retrieve and validate entity state value

Algorithm:
1. Validate pEntity pointer is not NULL
2. If NULL, assert with error code 0x240 and call non-returning error handler
3. Call Ordinal_10388 to process entity (side effects on entity state)
4. Load and return dword value from pEntity + offset 0x2c (entity state field)

Parameters:
pEntity (void*) - Pointer to entity structure (must not be NULL)

Returns:
dword - Entity state value from offset 0x2c in entity structure

Special Cases:
NULL pointer: Triggers assertion failure and non-returning error handler FUN_6fdd5a09
Magic Numbers: 0x2c (offset to state field), 0x240 (assertion error code)
Ordinal Calls: Ordinal_10388 performs entity state processing before retrieval

functions.name: Ordinal_10100
functions.comment:
Increment counter field in data structure.

Algorithm:
1. Check if pData pointer is non-NULL
2. If NULL, return immediately
3. Load DWORD value from offset 0x5c within structure
4. Increment value by 1
5. Store result back to offset 0x5c
6. Return

Parameters:
pData (void*) - Pointer to data structure (NULL-safe)

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
- NULL pointer is safe, returns without action
- Counter at 0x5c is DWORD (4 bytes)
- Called from Ordinal_10384

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x5c (92 decimal) - Offset of counter field within structure

functions.name: Ordinal_10036
functions.comment:
Accessor function for structure member at offset 0x5c with NULL safety check.

Algorithm:
1. Load parameter pData from stack at [ESP + 0x4]
2. Test if pData equals zero (NULL check)
3. If zero, return pData (0) immediately via RET
4. If non-zero, dereference [pData + 0x5c] as 32-bit signed integer
5. Return the dereferenced value via RET

Parameters:
pData (void *): Pointer to data structure containing the member to access, or NULL for safe early exit

Returns:
int: The 32-bit signed integer value at offset 0x5c within the data structure, or 0 if pData is NULL

Special Cases:
- NULL input returns 0 (defensive null checking pattern)
- No validation of pData before offset access

- Returns signed 32-bit value; caller must interpret based on context

functions.name: Ordinal_10101
functions.comment:
Decrement room reference counter (critical section exit) with validation.

Algorithm:
  1. Check if pRoom is NULL; if so, return immediately
  2. Load counter from pRoom->field_0x5c
  3. If counter < 1 (invalid/underflow state), trigger assertion with error context
  4. Call FUN_6fdd5a09(0xffffffff) which terminates execution
  5. Otherwise, decrement counter: pRoom->field_0x5c -= 1

Parameters:
  pRoom (Room*) - Pointer to room structure containing reference counter at offset 0x5c

Returns:
  void - Function returns normally unless counter underflow triggers assertion

Special Cases:
  - NULL pointer: skipped, no operation performed
  - Counter underflow: assertion failure at source line 0x273 (627 decimal) in D2Common.cpp
  - Counter valid: decremented by 1

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x5c - Offset to reference counter within Room structure
  0x273 - Line number in source file (627 decimal)
  0xffffffff (-1) - Termination error code passed to FUN_6fdd5a09

Related Functions:
  - D2Common_DbgAssertion() - Logs assertion failure before termination
  - FUN_6fdd5a09() - Terminates process with error code
  - Ordinal_10386() - Caller: removes unit from room, then decrements counter

functions.name: GetRoomDataFieldOffset
functions.comment:
Validates room offset and returns field offset pointer.

Algorithm:
1. Check if nRoomOffset parameter (ECX) is zero/NULL
2. If zero, call D2Common_DbgAssertion with file/line info and abort via FUN_6fdd5a09(-1)
3. If valid, calculate field offset: nRoomOffset + 0x2c
4. Return field offset in EAX

Parameters:
nRoomOffset (int): Room structure base offset; must be non-zero

Returns:
int: Field offset (nRoomOffset + 0x2c); non-returning on validation failure

Special Cases:
- Zero parameter triggers assertion and process termination
- Called by D2Common skill/spell ordinals
- Offset 0x2c represents field location within room structure

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x2c: Room structure field offset (44 bytes)
- 0x27d: Source line number for assertion
- 0xffffffff: Fatal error exit code

Related Functions:
- D2Common_DbgAssertion: Assertion handler
- FUN_6fdd5a09: Fatal error handler

functions.name: AllocateAndInitializeRoom
functions.comment:
Allocate and conditionally initialize room data structure.

Algorithm:
1. Test pRoom pointer for null condition
2. If pRoom is null, call D2Common_DbgAssertion with file/line/code information
3. Call FUN_6fdd5a09(-1) to terminate on assertion failure
4. Test nInitializeFlag for non-zero value
5. If nInitializeFlag is non-zero, dereference pRoom at offset 0x78
6. Access structure at [pRoom+0x78] and write 0x01 to offset 0x28
7. Load effective address of pRoom+0x30 into EAX
8. Return pointer to room data payload

Parameters:
pRoom - Pointer to Room structure (must not be null)
nInitializeFlag - Flag controlling initialization (0=skip, non-zero=initialize)

Returns:
Room * - Pointer to offset 0x30 within pRoom (data payload start address)

Special Cases:
- pRoom null check triggers assertion and program termination
- nInitializeFlag=0 skips field initialization
- Field at [pRoom+0x78+0x28] set to 0x01 when initialized

functions.name: Ordinal_10055
functions.comment:
Validate room pointer and set unit flag state.

Algorithm:
1. Check if nRoomPtr is null - if so, trigger assertion failure
2. If assertion fails, terminate process with error code -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)
3. Extract unit flag state from room structure at offset 0x38

functions.name: Ordinal_10099
functions.comment:
Find and return bit flag for matching item

Algorithm:
1. Call GetGameStateAndResult to retrieve pointer to item array and output count to dwCount
2. Initialize nIndex to 0
3. Loop while nIndex < dwCount:
   a. Compare current item at pCurrent with nItemId
   b. If match found, return bit flag (1 << nIndex) and exit
   c. Move pCurrent to next item (increment by sizeof(int))
   d. Increment nIndex
4. If no match found after loop, return 0

Parameters:
  nItemId (int) - Item value to search for in the array

Returns:
  int - Bit flag representing position if found (0x1 at index 0, 0x2 at index 1, etc), Returns 0 if no match found

Special Cases:
  - If count from GetGameStateAndResult is 0 or negative, loop is skipped and 0 is returned
  - Bit shifting is limited to 32-bit: (1 << 31) is maximum valid return for index 31

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x1f - Bit mask (31) used in CL register masking for shift operations
  0x4 - Size of each array element (4 bytes = 1 int)

Related Functions:

functions.name: InsertQueueElement

Inserts an element into a modulo-4 circular queue structure.

Algorithm:
1. Validate queue pointer (NULL check - early return if NULL)
2. Load write index from queue offset 0x64
3. Calculate target slot address: 0x68 + (index * 4)
4. Store element value at calculated offset
5. Increment write index
6. Wrap index using bitwise AND with 0x3 (modulo 4)
7. Write wrapped index back to queue offset 0x64
8. Return to caller

Parameters:

  dwElement: Value to insert into queue (uint).

Returns:

Special Cases:
  - Queue wraps from index 3 to 0
  - Oldest element is silently overwritten when full
  - No bounds checking or error codes

4. Calculate sum: (val2 + val1)

6. Scale sum by 8x and write back to pdwValue2

Parameters:
- pdwValue1: Pointer to first unsigned integer value
- pdwValue2: Pointer to second unsigned integer value

Returns:
-void (values modified in-place via pointers)

Algorithm:

2. Calculate difference: (A - B) * 5 * 16 = (A - B) * 80
3. Store scaled difference result in *pnValueA
4. Calculate sum: (A + B) * 5 * 16 / 2 = (A + B) * 40
5. Store scaled sum result in *pnValueB
6. Return (void)

Parameters:
- pnValueA (int *): Pointer to first integer operand
- pnValueB (int *): Pointer to second integer operand

Returns:
Void - Results stored via input pointers

Special Cases:
Function uses 2 stack temporaries (iVar1, iVar2) optimized away. Modifies values in-place.

functions.name: InitializeGameObjectState
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a 0x34-byte game object state structure with default configuration values.

OPTIMIZATION NOTE: Decompiler analysis generates synthetic variables (DVar1) from XMM register operations and temporaries eliminated during compilation. These cannot be renamed as they do not correspond to source-level variables.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x34 bytes (52 bytes) via memory allocator at 0x6fdd58da
2. Initialize allocated memory - zero all 0xD DWORDs (13 * 4 = 52 bytes) using REP STOSD
3. Set type field at offset +0x0 to 0x2 (initialized object indicator)
4. Load value from offset +0x2c (index), use as table lookup to [EAX*4 + g_pdwConfigTable]
5. Store looked-up value at offset +0x28 (configuration value)
6. Load conditional flag from offset +0x30; if zero use g_pdwConfigBase1, else g_pdwConfigBase2
7. Load multiplier from selected base (+0x0) and value (+0x4), store at +0x04
8. Load stored config value from +0x28, multiply by value at selected base, store result at +0x08
9. Call initialization subroutine 0x6fd9dd60 (pGameObj, 0) with pointer in ECX
10. Call initialization subroutine 0x6fd9deb0 (pGameObj, 0) with pointer in ECX
11. Clear field at offset +0x14 to 0x0
12. Call Ordinal_10045 (system time function) via function pointer at 0x6fddf12c, store result at +0x10
13. Clear final flag at offset +0x30 to 0x0
14. Return pointer in EAX

Parameters:
  None (no parameters)

Returns:
  EAX - Pointer to newly allocated and initialized 0x34-byte structure
        NULL on allocation failure (returned by allocator 0x6fdd58da)

Special Cases:
  Diablo II context: Function initializes game object state used throughout game loops
  Conditional initialization at algorithm step 6 based on external game state
  Field at offset +0x2c used as array index for configuration table lookup
  Ordinal_10045 call provides timestamp initialization (likely elapsed time since game start)

Structure Layout (0x34 bytes):
Offset | Size | Field Name     | Type   | Description
+0x00  | 0x4  | dwStateType    | DWORD  | Object state type (0x2 = initialized state)
+0x04  | 0x4  | dwMultiplier   | DWORD  | Configuration multiplier value from base
+0x08  | 0x4  | dwScaledValue  | DWORD  | Result of (g_pdwConfigTable[idx] * multiplier)
+0x0C  | 0x4  | (reserved)     | DWORD  | Zeroed padding field
+0x10  | 0x4  | dwTimestamp    | DWORD  | Timestamp from Ordinal_10045 system call
+0x14  | 0x4  | dwCounter      | DWORD  | Counter field (initialized to 0)
+0x18  | 0x8  | (reserved)     | QWORD  | Reserved or padding fields
+0x20  | 0x8  | (reserved)     | QWORD  | Reserved or padding fields
+0x28  | 0x4  | dwConfigValue  | DWORD  | Configuration value from g_pdwConfigTable lookup
+0x2C  | 0x4  | dwTableIndex   | DWORD  | Index for g_pdwConfigTable[dwTableIndex] lookup
+0x30  | 0x4  | dwCondFlag     | DWORD  | Conditional flag (cleared to 0x0 at end)

Related Functions:
- 0x6fd9dd60 - Initialization helper function 1
- 0x6fd9deb0 - Initialization helper function 2
- Ordinal_10045 - System timestamp/timing function (Fog.dll)

functions.name: AdjustRotationAngle
functions.signature: void AdjustRotationAngle(void * pViewport, int nKeyCode, int nMode)
functions.comment:
Summary: Adjusts rotation angle based on keyboard input and current viewport state

Algorithm:
1. Mode 3 handling (discrete angle adjustments):
   - Maps key codes (0x67/0x68/0x69/0x6a) to discrete angle values (0x80/0x40/0x38/0x30)
   - Increments or decrements current angle to approach target value
   - Special case: if angle is 0, jumps directly to target value
2. Normal mode handling (continuous angle calculation):
   - Key 0x78: Sets angle to fixed value 200
   - Otherwise: Calculates angle using trigonometry based on viewport dimensions
   - Computes cosine and sine of scaled angle for 3D rotation
   - Applies special multiplier if angle exceeds threshold (dimensions * 180)
   - Converts result to integer using __ftol
   - Clamps result to bounds: 0-0xff (mode 3) or 0-0xaa (mode 4)
3. Alternate path when viewport offset 0x30 is non-zero:
   - Decrements angle by 8 if above 0x20
   - Clamps minimum to 0x20

Parameters:
- pViewport: Pointer to viewport structure containing angle state and dimensions
  - Offset 0x08: input dimension value
  - Offset 0x0c: current angle value (modified by this function)
  - Offset 0x1c: cosine component (negative)
  - Offset 0x20: zero component
  - Offset 0x24: sine component
  - Offset 0x28: scaling dimension
  - Offset 0x30: alternate mode flag
- nKeyCode: Keyboard event code (0x67, 0x68, 0x69, 0x6a, or 0x78)
- nMode: Operation mode (3 = discrete steps, 4 = limited bounds, other = full range)

Returns: void (modifies pViewport structure in place)

Special Cases:
- Mode 3: Uses discrete angle increments rather than continuous calculation
- Key code 0x78: Forces angle to 200 regardless of other state
- Angle 0 in mode 3: Jumps directly to target instead of incrementing
- Angle > 180 degrees: Applies special sine multiplier

Magic Numbers:
- 0x67, 0x68, 0x69, 0x6a: Key codes for discrete angle selection
- 0x30, 0x38, 0x40, 0x80: Discrete angle target values (48, 56, 64, 128)
- 0xff (255): Maximum angle bound for mode 3
- 0xaa (170): Maximum angle bound for mode 4
- 0x78: Key code for reset to 200
- 0x20 (32): Minimum angle threshold in alternate path
- 8: Decrement step in alternate path
- 0xb4 (180): Threshold for special sine multiplier
- _DAT_6fde23c0, _DAT_6fde23b8, _DAT_6fde23b0: Trigonometric scaling constants

    Second call (if nAllocateItems==0): allocates 0x844 bytes for items list

4. Call validation function (0x6fdaacb0) with parameters
5. Test validation result: abValidResult[0] == 1 success
6. Iterate double loop: for nRowIdx = 0 to nRowCount-1
7. Inner loop: for nColIter = 0 to nColCount-1
8. Calculate cell offset: nCellOffset = base + nRowIdx*100 + nColIter*4 + 0x74
9. Check cell occupancy: if [[eBP+0x1c]+nCellOffset] != 0 skip search
10. Call search predicate (0x6fd9ec80) with search context
11. On match (return 1): write results to pOutRowIdx, pOutColIdx
12. On no match: return EAX=0
13. Assert on NULL pGridStruct (does not return)

  pOutRowIdx (int *): Output row index on successful match

  pOutColIdx (int *): Output column index on successful match
  pSearchCtx (int *): Search criteria context structure
  nColCount (byte): Number of columns in grid

Returns:

  EAX = 0: No unit matched search criteria

Magic Numbers:

  0x04, 0x1c: Structure member offsets for validation
  0x28: Grid cell element size (stride)
  0x100: Bytes per row (25 columns * 4)

functions.name: FindFreeGridSlot
functions.signature: uint FindFreeGridSlot(void * pGridOwner, uint * pDimensions, byte nOffsetX, uint nOffsetY, uint * pOutX, int * pOutY, uint nGridSize)
functions.comment:
PURPOSE:
Searches a 2D grid structure for the first available (empty) cell position that can accommodate
an item of the specified dimensions. The function iterates through the grid to find free slots,
checking for adequate contiguous space and returning the coordinates of a suitable location.

ALGORITHM:
1. Extract grid width from pDimensions[0] (low byte) and iterate columns from right to left (width-1 to 0)
2. Extract grid height from pDimensions[1] (low byte) and iterate rows from bottom to top (height-1 to 0)
3. For each cell position (uVar5, nY):
   a. Calculate grid cell pointer using offset: (x + (y + gridSize*10)*10)*4 + 0x74
   b. Access grid data through pGridOwner+0x1c (base grid array pointer)
   c. Check if cell at calculated offset is empty (value == 0)
4. If cell is empty, copy dimensions array (6 uints) to local buffer aDimsCopy
5. Validate item fits within grid bounds considering offsets:
   a. Check X boundary: (aDimsCopy[0] & 0xff) >= (nOffsetX + currentX)
   b. Check Y boundary: (aDimsCopy[0]>>8 & 0xff) >= (nOffsetY + currentY)
6. Iterate through required contiguous cells in nested loops (X: currentX to currentX+nOffsetX, Y: currentY to currentY+nOffsetY)
7. Verify all cells in range are empty by checking grid positions with stride:
   a. Row stride: 0x28 bytes (40 bytes, or 10 ints)
   b. Column stride: 0xa bytes (10 bytes, or 2.5 ints - likely 10 elements)
8. If all cells free, call FUN_6fd9ef20() to compute allocation priority/score
9. Store computed value in pResultCell grid lookup buffer (acStack_65 array indexed by [x + y*10 + 1])
10. If allocation score returns -1 (0xff), mark position as best candidate and return success
11. Continue iteration through all grid positions, tracking highest priority free slot
12. After all cells checked, return position with highest non-zero priority value

PARAMETERS:
pGridOwner    - void*  - Pointer to grid owner structure containing grid data array at offset +0x1c
pDimensions   - uint*  - Pointer to dimensions array (element 0 contains width/height packed as bytes)
nOffsetX      - byte   - X dimension/width of item to place in grid
nOffsetY      - uint   - Y dimension/height of item to place in grid (only low byte used)
pOutX         - uint*  - Output parameter receiving X coordinate of found free slot
pOutY         - int*   - Output parameter receiving Y coordinate of found free slot
nGridSize     - uint   - Grid size parameter used in cell offset calculation (only low byte used, multiplied by 10)

RETURNS:
uint - Returns 1 if a suitable free grid slot was found, 0 if no available space exists

SPECIAL CASES:
- Returns 0 immediately if no cells have any priority value (all slots occupied or invalid)
- Returns 1 with coordinates of highest priority slot when multiple options exist
- Grid is searched right-to-left, bottom-to-top (reverse iteration order)

MAGIC NUMBERS:
0x1c  - Offset within pGridOwner structure pointing to base grid data array
0x74  - Base offset added to calculated grid index (116 bytes, likely header size)
0x28  - Row stride in bytes (40 bytes = 10 int32 values per row)
0xa   - Column stride constant (10, used in nested grid calculations)
10    - Grid lookup buffer width (acStack_65 dimensioned as [y*10 + x + 1])
6     - Size of dimensions copy array (24 bytes = 6 uint values)

RELATED FUNCTIONS:
FUN_6fd9ef20 - Called to compute allocation priority/score for free grid positions

functions.name: CountOccurrencesInGrid
functions.signature: uint CountOccurrencesInGrid(int iContext, uint dwFlags, uint dwSize)
functions.comment:
Counts occurrences of non-zero values in a grid region with boundary expansion logic.

This function analyzes a 2D grid structure embedded within a context object and counts
non-zero integer values in a dynamically determined region. The region expands from a
starting position based on provided width/height parameters and boundary conditions.

Parameters:
  pContext - Pointer to context structure containing grid data at offset 0x1c
  byFlags - Flags byte affecting region calculation (bits used for width/height)
  wSize - Word containing packed size parameters (high/low bytes for dimensions)
  byWidth - Width dimension for the initial search region
  piHeight - Pointer to height value (passed on stack)
  iStartY - Starting Y coordinate for the grid search
  byLayer - Layer index multiplied by 10 for grid offset calculation

Returns:
  uint - Count of non-zero values found, or 0xFF if threshold exceeded

Algorithm:
  1. Extract grid pointer from context at offset 0x1c + 0x74
  2. Calculate initial region bounds using width/height and starting position
  3. Scan vertical strips checking for non-zero integer values at calculated offsets
  4. Expand search region based on boundary conditions (top/bottom/left/right)
  5. For each expanded region, recalculate grid offsets using formula:
     offset = ((row + (column + layer*10)*10) * 4
  6. Increment counter for each non-zero value found in grid
  7. Apply threshold check: if count >= (width+height)*2, return 0xFF
  8. Otherwise return actual count

Grid Structure:
  - Grid is accessed as int array at *(pContext+0x1c) + 0x74
  - Organized in 10x10 sections per layer
  - Each element is 4-byte integer
  - Layer offset: byLayer * 10
  - Row-major ordering with stride of 10

Edge Cases:
  - Returns 0xFF when count reaches/exceeds threshold (width+height)*2
  - Handles boundary expansion in 4 directions (vertical/horizontal)
  - Processes phantom stack variables for multi-dimensional indexing

functions.name: ValidateSlotIndices
functions.signature: int ValidateSlotIndices(int nIndex, uint * pDataArray, byte byThreshold, uint dwDimension, int * pOutIndex, int * pOutSlot, uint dwIterCount)
functions.comment:
Validates slot indices in multi-dimensional data array structure.

Algorithm:
1. Check if primary dimension size is zero; if so, skip validation
2. Copy primary dimension bounds to local buffer using MOVSD
3. Iterate through each primary slot (outer loop)
4. For each primary slot:
   a. Calculate offset into data array using dimension multiplier
   b. Load pointer to element at calculated offset
   c. If element is null, process next primary slot
   d. Copy data bounds and validate against thresholds
5. Validate range: primary_index + param3 <= primary_bounds
6. Validate range: secondary_index + param1 <= secondary_bounds
7. For valid ranges, iterate through all slots in range
8. Check each element for validity (non-zero)
9. If all slots valid, call helper function at 0x6fd9ef20 with slot data
10. Store result index and slot in output pointers if successful
11. Scan secondary dimension for maximum value
12. Return 1 if valid slot found, 0 otherwise

Parameters:
  nIndex: int - Primary dimension index or counter
  pDataArray: uint* - Pointer to multi-dimensional data array
  byThreshold: byte - Primary dimension validation threshold
  dwDimension: uint - Secondary dimension size
  pOutIndex: int* - Output: validated primary index
  pOutSlot: int* - Output: validated slot identifier
  dwIterCount: uint - Iteration limit for secondary dimension

Returns:

functions.name: InitializeMapTileArray
functions.signature: void InitializeMapTileArray(uint dwWidth, uint dwHeight, int nStartRow, uint dwRowCount, uint dwFlags, uint dwBaseOffset)
functions.comment:
InitializeMapTileArray - Initialize multidimensional map tile array with zero values

Algorithm:
1. Save registers (ESI, EDI, EBX, EBP) for callee-save convention
2. Validate input: Call validation function at 0x6fd9fbd0 with assembly parameters
3. If validation fails (EAX == 0), log line 0x483 to D2Common error log, then exit with -1
4. Call secondary initialization at 0x6fdaacb0 to prepare structures/offsets
5. Validate base pointer (EDI) is non-NULL; if NULL log line 0x177, exit with -1
6. Validate base pointer offset structure (EDI + 0x1c) is non-NULL; if NULL log line 0x178, exit with -1
7. Extract lower byte of dwWidth, add to base row index to get end row
8. Outer loop: For each row from nStartRow to (nStartRow + dwRowCount - 1):
   9. Extract lower byte of dwHeight as inner loop limit
   10. Inner loop: For each column from base column to (base column + dwHeight - 1):
       11. Calculate offset: (dwFlags & 0xFF) * 10 + nStartRow * 2 + column * 2 + 0x74
       12. Add base array pointer offset (EDI + 0x1c)
       13. Increment by 4 bytes, zero DWORD, repeat for each column
   14. Advance base row by dwRowCount
9. Restore registers and return via __stdcall (RET 0x18 pops 6 parameters)

Parameters:
- dwWidth: uint - Array width (lower 8 bits used), specifies column count
- dwHeight: uint - Array height (lower 8 bits used), specifies row iteration count
- nStartRow: int - Starting row index for initialization loop
- dwRowCount: uint - Number of rows to process in outer loop
- dwFlags: uint - Flags value, lower 8 bits used in offset calculation (factor of 10)
- dwBaseOffset: uint - Base memory offset or array base address

Returns:
- void (modifies memory in-place)
- Exits with -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) on validation failure (calls 0x6fdd5a09)

Special Cases:
- Validates all parameters through function call at 0x6fd9fbd0
- Falls through validation failure logging to 0x6fdd58d4 before exit
- Requires valid base pointer (EDI) and base offset structure pointer (EDI + 0x1c)
- Uses only lower 8 bits of dwWidth, dwHeight, and dwFlags for calculations
- Loop structure uses 16-bit increment per column (offset += 4, writes DWORD)

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x483: Error code 1155 (decimal) - Initial validation failure
- 0x486: Error code 1158 (decimal) - Structure initialization marker
- 0x177: Error code 375 (decimal) - Invalid base pointer
- 0x178: Error code 376 (decimal) - Invalid offset structure
- 0xFF: Byte mask for parameter extraction
- 0x1c: Offset into base pointer structure for array data
- 0x74: Array offset bias constant

Algorithm:
1. Validate pInventory pointer is non-NULL, assert if NULL
2. Load list head from [pInventory + 0x28]
3. Return 0 if list head is NULL
4. Initialize fFound = false
5. For each node in linked list via offset 0x10:
   a. Return 0 if node is NULL
   b. If dwSelector provided (non-zero), verify [node + 0x4] == dwSelector
   c. If mismatch, advance to next node

   e. Check [node + 0xc] == 0x3 (entry type validation)

   g. Compare result with dwSelector parameter
   h. If mismatch, advance to next node
   i. Call Ordinal_10519 with 0x46 and node ID
   j. Call Ordinal_10795 with node ID
   k. If capacity check passes, return [node + 0x4]
   l. Advance to [node + 0x10], repeat

Parameters:

- dwSelector (uint): Item selector ID to match (0 = no filtering)
- dwFilterCriteria (uint): Secondary filter parameter

- 0 if list empty, no match found, or validation fails

| 0x28 | 4 | list_head | Node* | First item node in list |

Item node structure:

| 0x4 | 4 | item_id | uint | Item identifier |
| 0xc | 4 | type | int | Item type (must equal 0x3) |
| 0x10 | 4 | next | Node* | Next item node pointer |

Special Cases:
- NULL pInventory triggers debug assertion
- Empty list (NULL at 0x28) returns 0
- dwSelector = 0 disables selector filtering
- Type field [0xc] must equal exactly 0x3 for validation
- Magic constant 0x46 used in capacity validation

functions.signature: int * FindEquippedItemAfterPosition(int * pInventory, int nItemRef, int * pPositionMarker)
functions.comment:
Searches for an equipped/wearable item in an inventory's linked list after a position marker.

Algorithm:
  1. Validates inventory pointer (pInventory != NULL) - asserts and exits if invalid
  2. Starts traversal at pInventory+0x28 (inventory item list head)
  3. Iterates through linked list using +0x10 offset for next node pointer

  7. Verifies item's parent inventory matches the search inventory
  8. Returns pointer to matching item node or NULL if not found

Parameters:
  pInventory - Pointer to inventory structure (validated non-NULL, contains item list at +0x28)
  nItemRef - Item reference/ID passed to ResolveItemDataOffset for validation
  pPositionMarker - Pointer to item node to start search after, or 0 to search from beginning

Returns:

  NULL (0) if no matching equipped item found or end of list reached

Special Cases:
  - If pInventory is NULL: Triggers assertion and FUN_6fdd5a09(0xffffffff) termination
  - If ResolveItemDataOffset validation fails: Triggers assertion and termination
  - If pPositionMarker is 0/NULL: Searches entire list from beginning
  - Empty inventory or no items after marker: Returns NULL gracefully

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x28 - Offset to item linked list head in inventory structure
  0x04 - Offset to item data pointer in node structure
  0x0c - Offset to item type field in node structure
  0x10 - Offset to next node pointer in linked list
  0x03 - Item type value for equipped/wearable items
  0x84e - Assertion line number for null inventory validation

functions.signature: byte ProcessTileOrMobData(int * pnParam1, int nParam2, int * pnParam3)
functions.comment:
ProcessTileOrMobData - Process and cache tile/mob item data

SUMMARY:
Validates input parameters (unit, item, save header) and processes tile/mob data by
caching item codes in a global cache structure. The cache maps item types to slot indices
for quick lookup during game operations.

Algorithm:
1. Validate three input parameters (unit pointer, save header, item pointer) - assert if NULL
2. Get item type from item pointer (must be type 4 or 5 - tile or mob drops)
3. For tile items (type 0x20776278):
   a. Get item properties and validate item sub-type (5 or 6)
   b. Initialize global cache structure at 0x6fe04658 on first use (254 slots)
   c. Pre-populate cache with known item codes
   d. Scan all items in item database and cache valid item codes
   e. Search cache for matching item code and return slot index (1-254) or 0xff if not found
   f. Store slot index in save header at offset +0x2c
4. For bow items (type 0x20776f62):
   a. Resolve item data offset for til key
   b. Get item codes from resolved data
   c. Search cache for matching item code
   d. Store slot index in save header at offset +0x2b
5. Return status byte indicating cache slot or 0xff for no match

Parameters:
- pnParam1: Pointer to unit structure (ECX register, __fastcall)
- nParam2: Save header structure address (EDX register, __fastcall)
- pnParam3: Pointer to item structure (stack parameter)

Returns:
- byte: Status/result code - cache slot index or operation result, 0xff if not found

functions.name: DecodeCoordinateData
functions.signature: int DecodeCoordinateData(uint dwEncodedCoords, int nParam, uint * pdwX, int * pnY, int * pnLayer)
functions.comment:
Decodes packed coordinate data into X, Y, and layer indices.

ALGORITHM:
1. Extract X coordinate: X = dwEncodedCoords & 0x3 (bits 0-1, 0-3)
2. Extract Y coordinate: Y = ((dwEncodedCoords >> 2) & 0x3FF) - 0x100 (bits 2-11)
3. Extract layer: layer = ((dwEncodedCoords >> 12) & 0x3FF) - 0x100 (bits 12-21)
4. Compute distance: abs(nParam - X), clamped [0, 2]
5. Store outputs if pointers non-null
6. Return: (layer - Y) * (distance / 2) - X

PARAMETERS:
dwEncodedCoords (uint) - Packed 32-bit coordinate data
nParam (int) - Reference value
pdwX (uint*) - Output X (0-3)
pnY (int*) - Output Y coordinate
pnLayer (int*) - Output layer index

RETURNS:
int - Computed offset: (layer - Y) * (distance / 2) - X

functions.name: ComputeQuotientRemainder3
functions.signature: uint ComputeQuotientRemainder3(uint dwValue, uint * pQuotient3, uint * pRemainder3, uint * pShiftAmount)
functions.comment:
Compute quotient and remainder by dividing 5-bit fields by 3

Algorithm:
1. Validate all parameters non-NULL (param_1, param_2, param_3, param_4) via TEST instructions
2. Extract lower 5 bits of param_1 via AND 0x1F
3. Multiply by magic constant 0x55555556 (implements division by 3)
4. Perform signed division: result >> 31, add EDX, get signed quotient
5. Divide result by 3 using IDIV to get final quotient
6. Store quotient in *param_2 via MOV [EBX], EDX
7. Shift param_1 right by 5 bits using SAR instruction
8. Mask shifted value with 0x1F to get 5-bit result
9. Store result in *param_3 via MOV [EDI], ECX
10. Store final masked shift in *param_4
11. Return via RET 0x10 (stdcall cleanup)

Parameters:
param_1 (dwValue) - Input value containing 5-bit bitfields to process
param_2 (pQuotient3) - Pointer to quotient result (low 5 bits / 3)
param_3 (pRemainder3) - Pointer to remainder result (low 5 bits % 3)
param_4 (pShiftAmount) - Pointer to masked high bits ((param_1 >> 5) & 0x1F)

Returns:
Success via RET 0x10 on valid parameters
Process abort via error handler at 0x6fda30c1 on NULL parameter

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1F = 31 decimal - 5-bit mask (binary: 0001_1111)
0x55555556 = 1431655766 - magic constant for efficient division by 3
0x3 = 3 - divisor for quotient/remainder computation
0x5 = 5 bits - bitfield width and shift amount

4. Calculate final base contribution: nBaseValue * 2

- nMultiplier (int): Scaling factor multiplied by 32 from stack offset 0xc

Returns:

Special Cases:

functions.signature: int GenerateRandomInRange(int * pRandState, int nMin, int nMax)
functions.comment:
/****************************************************************************
 * FUNCTION: GenerateRandomInRange
 *
 * SUMMARY:
 * Generates a random integer in the range [nMin, nMax] using the game's
 * random number generator. This function is used throughout D2Common.dll
 * for procedural generation of items, maps, and game mechanics.
 *
 * ALGORITHM:
 * 1. Track if nMin is negative (store sign in bNegMin)
 * 2. If nMin is negative, negate it to make positive
 * 3. Track if nMax is negative (store sign in bNegMax)
 * 4. If nMax is negative, negate it to make positive
 * 5. Assert that nMax >= nMin (call Ordinal_10312 if violated)
 * 6. Get random inclusivity flag from pRandState[1] (wRandFlag)
 * 7. Cast wRandFlag to short and compare with 0
 * 8. Compute dwCount = (nMax - nMin) + (wRandFlag ? 1 : 0)
 * 9. Call Ordinal_10918(pRandState, dwCount) to get random value
 * 10. Add nMin to random result: nResult = random + nMin
 * 11. Verify nResult <= nMax (assert via Ordinal_10312)
 * 12. Apply original sign: if bNegMin was set, negate nResult
 * 13. Return final signed result
 *
 * PARAMETERS:
 * @param pRandState  - Pointer to random state array (passed in ECX register)
 *                      Used by Ordinal_10691 and Ordinal_10918 for RNG
 * @param nMin        - Minimum value of range (inclusive, passed in EDX)
 * @param nMax        - Maximum value of range (inclusive, passed on stack)
 *
 * RETURNS:
 * @return int - Random integer in range [nMin, nMax] with proper sign
 *
 * SPECIAL CASES:
 * - If nMin == nMax, returns that value (dwCount = 0 or 1 depending on flag)
 * - Handles negative ranges by tracking sign and normalizing to positive
 * - Asserts nMax >= nMin, will fail if range is invalid
 * - Random inclusivity controlled by wRandFlag (makes max inclusive/exclusive)
 *
 * MAGIC NUMBERS:
 * - pRandState[1]: Random inclusivity flag (0 = exclusive max, 1 = inclusive max)
 * - Ordinal_10691: Get pointer to random array (returns ulonglong*)
 * - Ordinal_10918: Generate random number in range [0, dwCount)
 * - Ordinal_10312: Assertion function, terminates if condition false
 *
 * CALLING CONVENTION: __fastcall
 * - ECX: pRandState (first parameter)
 * - EDX: nMin (second parameter)
 * - Stack: nMax (third parameter)
 ****************************************************************************/

4. Return calculated offset in EAX register

- Offset calculation uses 0x10 (16) byte field spacing for each property
- Base offset 0x44 (68) bytes from item data structure start
- Both param_1 and nPropertyIndex must be valid or function asserts and terminates

0x10 (16): Size of each property field in bytes

0xffffffff (-1): Assertion failure code passed to FUN_6fdd5a09 terminator

functions.name: ProcessUnitSkills
functions.signature: void ProcessUnitSkills(UnitAny * pUnit, void * pContext, int nSkillCount)
functions.comment:
Process skill slots for a unit, initializing or validating skill data in two arrays.

Algorithm:
1. Validate parameter: if nSkillCount == 0, log error and exit
2. Retrieve unit object: call function at 0x6fdaffb0(pContext)
3. Fetch unit data: call function at 0x6fd73460(result) to get pRetUnit
4. If pRetUnit is NULL, exit
5. Read skill limit from pRetUnit+0x64: nMax = pRetUnit[0x64], decrement by 1
6. Clamp skill count: nSkillLimit = MIN(nSkillCount, nMax-1)
7. If nSkillLimit > 0:
  a. Loop through first skill array (offset 0x494) from index 0x2a to nSkillLimit
  b. Check if skill slot is valid ([Edi] >= 0)
  c. If valid: call 0x6fda7930 with parameters
8. Loop through second skill array (offset 0x4d4)
9. For each slot index 0x2e to 0x34:
  a. Check slot validity
  b. Process skill if valid

Parameters:
-pUnit: UnitAny * (IMPLICIT ECX) - Pointer to unit structure containing skill data
-pContext: void * (IMPLICIT EDX) - Context pointer for data retrieval
-nSkillCount: int - Number of skills to process (0x40 max)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
-If nSkillCount == 0: Error logged at line 0x6fa
-If pRetUnit is NULL: Early return, no processing
-If nSkillCount > 0x40: Clamped to 0x40 by comparison at 0x6fda7ae4
-Array bounds protection: loops verify each slot ([Edi] >= 0)

Magic Numbers:
-0x64: Offset in UnitAny storing max skill count
-0x494: Offset of first skill array (usually active skills)
-0x4d4: Offset of second skill array (usually passive skills)
-0x2a (0x2e): Starting indices for skill loops
-0x34: Upper bound for skill indices
-0x40: Maximum skill count limit

functions.name: Ordinal_10863
functions.comment:

functions.name: FindItemInTable
functions.comment:
FindItemInTable - Search item table for matching entry

Algorithm:
1. Validate nSearchItem parameter is not NULL (assert if NULL)
2. Initialize nLastMatch = -1 (not found), nMatchCount = 0
3. Point pCurrentEntry to start of global item table g_pItemTable
4. Loop through item table entries from g_pItemTable (0x6fde2574) to 0x6fde259c:
   a. Call Ordinal_10520 comparison function with nSearchItem and current table entry
   b. If comparison returns <= 0, break loop (no match found)
   c. Otherwise, store current table entry value as nLastMatch
   d. Advance pCurrentEntry to next table entry (increment by 4 bytes)
   e. Increment nMatchCount
5. After loop, check if pResult pointer is valid (not NULL)
6. If pResult is valid and nMatchCount < 10:
   a. Store result at pResult location: *pResult = g_pItemTable[nMatchCount]
7. If nMatchCount >= 10:
   a. Set *pResult = -1 (error condition - too many matches)
8. Return nLastMatch value (last matched item, or -1 if no match)

Parameters:
- nSearchItem: Integer search criteria (item ID or type code to search for)
- pResult: Output pointer where matched result will be stored (may be NULL if caller does not need result stored)

Returns:
- int: Value of last matched item from table, or -1 if no match found

Notes:
- Table range is fixed at compile time: 10 entries from 0x6fde2574 to 0x6fde259c (40 bytes total, 10 dword entries)
- Uses Ordinal_10520 as comparison/matching function to determine if items match search criteria
- Result is conditionally stored only if match count is less than 10 (validates array bounds)
- Function tracks count of matches but returns only the last matching value
- If more than 10 matches occur, sets error result but still returns last match value

  - Loop counter range 0xcc-0xd5 (204-213) skips invalid indices

functions.name: Ordinal_10815
functions.comment:
Returns maximum ability rank for a unit.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input unit pointer is not NULL, log error 0x114c if NULL
2. Verify unit type field (offset +0x00) equals 0x4, log error 0x114d if mismatch
3. Load field at offset +0x04, validate via function 0x6fd6f0d0, log 0x1143 if invalid
4. Extract base_rank from unit offset +0x3a
5. Check unit type: if != 0x4 return error code 0x01
6. Else for type 0x4: Load unit reference at offset +0x04
7. Validate reference via 0x6fd6f0d0, extract ability_ref from offset +0x26
8. Call 0x6fd75530 to get context/capacity structure
9. Validate capacity field at offset +0x00 against ability_ref, log 0x115a if exceeded
10. Branch on ability_ref value for rank lookup:
    - If ability_ref <= 0x19: calculate index, read capacity offset +0x22
    - If ability_ref <= 0x28: calculate index, read capacity offset +0x23
    - Else (> 0x28): calculate index, read capacity offset +0x24
11. Return maximum of base_rank vs selected_rank in AL

Parameters:
pUnit (int *) - Unit structure pointer
  Offset +0x00: unit type field (must be 0x4 for unit entity)
  Offset +0x04: unit reference/data pointer
  Offset +0x3a: base ability rank (byte)
  Offset +0x70: optional data field (checked for type 0x4)

Returns:
AL - Maximum ability rank (byte) from comparison of base_rank vs selected_rank
0x01 - Error return if unit type field != 0x4

Special Cases:
- Magic Number 0x19 (25 decimal) - Lower ability rank threshold
- Magic Number 0x28 (40 decimal) - Upper ability rank threshold  
- Magic Number 0x3a - Offset to base ability rank in unit
- Magic Number 0x26 - Offset to ability reference in unit data
- Magic Number 0x22, 0x23, 0x24 - Rank lookup offsets in capacity structure by ability range
- Index calculation: ability_ref * 30 - ability_ref = ability_ref * 29
- Error codes: 0x114c (NULL unit), 0x114d (wrong type), 0x1143 (invalid reference), 0x4e5/0x4e6 (data access), 0x4e0 (fallback), 0x7dc (2nd validation), 0x115a (capacity exceeded)
